commands.description: Open the About dialog (non-modally) - Help > About dispatches this. app.version answers the same facts as data.

Answer a question about the program from what it ships: the manual's sections and every command's description, best match first ({kind: manual|command, id, title, text, score}; a manual id is an app.help topic, a command id can be run). 'limit' answers (5 when left out, at most 20). Offline: nothing is sent anywhere.

Open the manual inside the application - at 'topic' (quickstart, window, arrange, notes, mix, devices, record, launch, workflows, projects, agents, customise, access) - or, with 'reference', the command reference: every command with its description and arguments, built from the registry and grouped by the manual's sections, found by 'query' when given (a name, a task, a shortcut or a word) - or, with 'whats_this', What's This? mode: the next click on a control shows its full description - or, with 'context' (F1), help for the control with the keyboard focus, needing no hover: the manual at its section with what the control is, the command it runs by name and its shortcut ('context' in the reply). Interface state.

Open the online documentation in the system browser - Help > Online Help dispatches this. It hands a URL to the desktop, which opens a program outside this one, so it declares `requires: human`: an unattended caller is refused rather than having a browser launched for it. `url` is where it points.
Cancel background task 'id' (as app.tasks lists it): a render-queue job, the library scan or a stem separation job.

Every background task in one list - render-queue jobs, the library scan, stem separation jobs and auto-mastering - each with an id, kind, state, label and progress (0..1 where it is known); 'active_only' keeps the queued and running ones.
Start a guided tour ('name', as app.tours lists it): each step points at a part of the window - showing its panel first when it is hidden - with Back, Next and Close. Interface state.
The guided tours there are: each one's name, title and step count.
The product name, the version string, the control protocol version and the build options the binary was compiled with.

The release notes the program ships for this version ('notes': version, title, items), every version's ('all'), and whether they have been shown here ('seen'; window.whats_new shows them, and the interface does so once per version at start). Nothing is fetched: there is no update check.

Give every track the height that fits them all in the arranger's height (clamped to 32..256 px), or the 'heights' given, in track order. Track heights are saved with the project, so this is one undo step.

Every track with its clips, addressed by the stable trk-<n> and clip-<n> ids. The trk-<n> number is assigned at creation and persists in the project file. Addressing is scoped to the SONG container: a track inside a nested container (the <trackcontainer> a pattern track carries) is not reachable by id, exactly as it is not addressable by index. `playhead_ticks` reports the arranger's Song-timeline position, also used by the video window.

The arranger's editing modes, set and answered: 'ripple' (off, track, all - a deletion closes its gap on the clip's track or on every track), 'overlap' (free, trim, crossfade - what a clip moved onto others does to them; trim by default, and never to a locked clip: such a move is refused), 'snap_to_edges' (moving a clip also snaps to other clips' edges and to markers) and 'automation_follows_clips' (a clip's move carries the points of the automation lanes following its track) and 'auto_fade_ms' (0..50: every sample clip fades in and out over at least that long, so no edit clicks; 0 off) and 'show_transients' (sample clips mark their audio's hits) and 'snap_to_zero_crossings' (a split or trim of a sample clip - the knife, clip.split, clip.trim - moves to the nearest zero crossing within 10 ms, frame-exact). The arranger's gestures and clip.move / clip.delete / range.delete follow them. An editing preference kept in the config file, not project state.

Bind a second arranger tool to a modifier key: while 'alt', 'ctrl' or 'shift' is held over the arranger, its tool is the one named (draw, knife, select, range, audition, zoom, smart), and letting go puts the previous tool back. An empty name unbinds the key. A preference (config ui/modifiertools); none by default. Reports the bindings.
Show or hide the navigator under the arranger ('visible'), the whole song in miniature with the part on screen outlined. A preference (config ui/navigator); with no arguments it reports it.
Move the play position to the next (or, with 'direction' previous, the previous) transient of the audio clips under it - tab to transient. Through transport.seek.
Move the selected clip left or right by 'amount' ticks (default: the arranger's snap) - clip.move, which records itself. Refused when the clip is already at the start.

Show or hide the arranger's ruler lanes under the bar ruler: 'sections' (named bands), 'markers' (flags and names), 'tempo' (the tempo map's curve and values) and 'chords' (the chord track's chords, which takes room only while the chord track holds one). A lane left out keeps its state; with no arguments it reports them. A preference (config ui/rulerlanes; all four shown by default), not project state.
Scroll the arranger so it starts at 'position' (ticks) - the navigator's click. Reports the position it reached and how many ticks the arranger shows. Interface state; nothing in the project changes.
Select the next or previous clip on the selected clip's track (window.select). Interface state.

Choose the arranger's tool: draw, knife, select, range, audition, zoom or smart. Beyond the song editor's draw / knife / select: range (draws time ranges, range.set), audition (plays from the pressed point while held, the pressed track alone), zoom (the dragged span fills the width) and smart (a clip's upper half draws a range, its lower half moves). Interface state.

Zoom the arranger: to 'pixels_per_bar', by 'step' zoom steps (negative zooms out), to the span 'start'..'end' (the zoom tool's drag), or to 'fit' the song, the loop or the selection (the time range, else the selected clips) across its width (scrolled to its start). A 'pixels_per_bar' or 'step' zoom keeps one tick where it is on screen ('anchor' in the answer): 'anchor_tick' (a pointer gesture passes the tick under the pointer), else 'anchor' - selection, playhead, view (its middle), start (its left edge) or auto (the default: the selection, else the playhead when it is on screen, else the middle). The previous zoom joins the history arrangement.zoom_back walks back over. Interface state.

Go back one step in the zoom history, to an earlier extent - the same way the browser goes back, to walk back over several prior extents. A new arrangement.zoom cuts what can be walked forward off; the selection, else the playhead on screen, stays where it is. Refused when there is nothing earlier.

Go forward one step in the zoom history, back over what arrangement.zoom_back went past (the way the browser goes forward). The selection, else the playhead on screen, stays where it is. Refused when there is nothing later.

Swap the arranger's zoom with the extent it last left (the zoom before this one, or the extent a back or forward step left behind), so pressing the toggle twice returns to where you were. The selection, else the playhead on screen, stays where it is. Refused before any second extent is known.

The audio backends this build knows, with the one that is running and the one the config file selects. Requires no audio device: the running name is whatever the engine opened, the dummy device when nothing else would open.

Choose the audio backend for the next start: the device name is written to the config file's audioengine/audiodev, the same key the settings dialog writes. The running device is NOT switched - the engine constructs its device in AudioEngine::initDevices() during startup and the product's own settings dialog also only stores the preference and warns that a restart is needed. The result says so explicitly with applied="next_start".

The audio interface's channels: how many outputs and inputs the running device opened ('granted') against what its I/O setup asks for ('requested'), every channel's name, the stereo and mono buses, and what is routed to each output (channels' hardware outputs, insert sends, cue mixes). 'multichannel' false: this backend opens a stereo pair only, and routes beyond outputs 1/2 play nowhere. Read only.

Set up the running device's interface channels - machine settings, kept per device, not in the project. 'outputs' and 'inputs' each take 'names' (one per channel, from channel 1; an empty one is left alone) and 'buses' ([{name, channels: "3/4" or "5"}], replacing the buses; a bus is stereo or mono, buses may not overlap and their names must differ); 'outputs' also takes 'channels', how many outputs to open (1..128, 2 by default), which takes effect when the device is next opened (JACK and ALSA; PortAudio opens what its own setup names). The input count is the capture plan's (record.input_set). One undo step.

Add or replace one automation point (ticks, value) on a track's device parameter. The value is the model's own unit and is range-checked against the model's own min..max. Creates the automation clip when the parameter has none yet, and says so: that first call is the one control.undo cannot fully reverse (the new AutomationTrack has no journal checkpoint). Later calls are reversible.

A trim lane: a RELATIVE clip under the track whose distance from the middle of the parameter's range is added to what the parameter's own automation (or its value) says - the offset curve of trim automation. One undo step.
Remove every automation point from a parameter's clip, leaving the clip bound to the model (an empty clip no longer drives the parameter). Reversible through the ProjectJournal.

Replace a parameter's points between 'start' and 'end' (song ticks) with a shape - sine, triangle, square, saw, random or adsr - over 'cycles' periods between 'min' and 'max' (the parameter's own units; default its range), a point every 'step' ticks ('seed' repeats random). One undo step.

Set the automation editor's edit mode: draw (add and move points), erase (remove them), draw_out_values (draw a curve's out-values directly) or edit_tangents (shape the tangents of a cubic Hermite curve - refused, typed, for any other progression, exactly as the toolbar's own disabled button says). The toolbar's matching button is checked afterwards and 'previous' reports the mode it was in. The mode is interface state: it is not saved with the project and has no undo.

Per track, every automatable device parameter with its stable '<plugin>/<index>' id, its current automation 'mode' (what automation.mode_set sets) and, for each automated one, its clip's points and record flag. A point's 'value' is the model's own unit (what plugin.param_get reports); 'raw_value' is what the clip stores. 'automated_only' trims the inventory.

A lane for one of a track's parameters (automation.get_state names them): an automation track placed right under the track, following it (its points move with the track's clips when arrangement.modes says so), with a clip across the song starting at the parameter's value. One undo step.

Fold or unfold a track's child automation lanes in the arranger: with 'collapsed' true every lane following the track (an AutomationTrack whose followsTrack is this track) is hidden under its owner's row, exactly as a collapsed folder hides its children. A live Track checkpoint, so one control.undo takes the fold back off; automation.get_state reports each owner's flag and each lane's owner. One undo step.
The parameter a person or a command last changed (not the automation): its track and parameter ids, ready for automation.lane_add.

Latency-compensated automation: with 'enabled' true every automation clip is read where the audio it moves is - its curve shifted later by the latency upstream of its parameter (the devices before it in its chain, plus its mixer channel's PDC alignment), so a move lands on the sound it was drawn on. Saved with the project only while on (older projects render as before). With no arguments it reports it, with how many clips read with a lag. One undo step.

Set a parameter's automation mode: off (ignore the curve - the manual value stands and nothing is written), read (follow the curve, never write), touch (write while the control is held, then return to reading), latch (write from the first touch until the transport run ends), or write (overwrite the pass while the transport runs). The mode is runtime state: not persisted and not journalled, so it has no undo. automation.get_state reports each parameter's mode, so the change can be observed and not only issued.
Move the automation point at 'ticks' to 'new_ticks' and/or 'new_value' (the control's own unit, range-checked) - what the automation editor's arrow keys and drags send. One undo step.

Per automated parameter: the sample-accuracy mode its clip asked for, and the ramp the audio thread built for it in the last rendered block - knots, frames, whether the value MOVES inside the block, and how many knots the fixed capacity had to refuse. Entries are read from the clips themselves, on every track the engine plays automation from (including the hidden global automation track), so 'track' is the target the parameter is addressed by ('ch-<n>'/'trk-<n>', the one ramp_set takes) and 'parameter' its '<plugin>/<index>' id: the pair addresses the parameter back. 'track' filters on that target, and 'include_block_mode' false trims it to the parameters asking for sample accuracy. 'unaddressable_object_count' counts the clip objects the surface has no parameter id for (the song's tempo, a pattern-internal control) rather than dropping them silently.

Render one automation clip at SAMPLE precision inside each audio block ('sample'), or block-quantised ('block'). With neither set (ramp_get's mode_source 'default') a clip carrying a curve is 'sample' and a Discrete (stepped) one 'block' - the default since R1.2. In 'sample' mode the parameter's per-sample buffer - what the mixer, the fx chain and the tracks multiply their samples with - carries the curve at every frame instead of one value smeared over the whole block. Reversible through the ProjectJournal.

Set a parameter's automation clip record flag: 'on' to write the control's manual value into the clip at every tick the transport runs, 'off' to stop. The clip is a JournallingObject, so the inverse is a live checkpoint.
Remove the automation point at an exact tick. The node list is a map keyed by tick, so the tick must match one. Reversible through the ProjectJournal.
Give the point at 'ticks' its own curve to the next point: clip (the clip's progression), hold, linear, smooth or bend ('bend' -1..1). One undo step.

Switches over all automation at once, on top of each control's own mode: 'read' off keeps every control at its manual value, 'write' off stops every control recording, 'punched_writes' records only inside the transport's punch region. Saved with the project when not at their defaults. With no arguments it reports them. One undo step.
Remove the points of a parameter that lie within 'tolerance' of the line through their kept neighbours (Douglas-Peucker; the first and last stay). One undo step.

Rescale a parameter's points between 'start' and 'end': in time about 'start' ('time_scale', then 'time_offset' ticks) and in value about the middle of its range ('value_scale', then 'value_offset'). One undo step.
A control's trim: the offset added to its written automation as it plays.

Set a control's trim - an offset (in the control's own unit) added to its written automation as it plays, never written into the clip, so the curve's shape stays and the whole of it moves. Runtime state like the automation mode (not saved). One undo step.

Write to end: from 'ticks' (song ticks) to the song's end the control holds 'value' (its own unit, range-checked; its current value when left out). Every later point is removed, the point at 'ticks' steps from the curve's value there to the new one, and a point at the song's end (the end of its last clip) holds it - what a write pass leaves to the end. Creates the automation clip when the control has none. Answers {track, parameter, ticks, end, value, removed, automation}. One undo step.

Render one track's own output - its devices, fader, pan and sends, which is what a stem is - to a WAV file and return the file, its frame count and its sha256. With 'start' and 'end' (ticks) the file covers that region instead of the whole track. The session is NOT modified: the render runs in a child process against a serialised copy with every other track muted, so nothing in this instance changes and nothing is journalled. The track menu's Bounce in place runs it; bounce.land is the verb that also puts the render on a new audio track. This command keeps its synchronous result contract for compatibility; use render.queue_bounce for a cancellable background job.

Bounce a track in place, the way a DAW's 'bounce to audio' does: render its own output (as bounce.in_place does, the whole track or 'start'/'end' ticks) and put the render on a NEW audio track at the range's start, named '<track> (bounce)', with the source track muted. Reversible: one control.undo removes the new track and restores the source's mute. bounce.in_place stays the render-only verb; freeze.track plays a render on the source track itself. This command keeps its synchronous result contract for compatibility; use render.queue_bounce with operation bounce_land for a cancellable job.

Show a list in the browser and remember it: runs 'command' (browser.query, browser.index_query, browser.collection_run or browser.similar) with 'args', answers its result, and adds it to the browser's history ('label' is what the history shows) - or, with 'replace', puts it in place of the current entry (a search refined as it is typed). A step after going back drops the forward history.

The category vocabulary of the library (0.5.0 L11, WF-007): every distinct category a file carries, with the number of files carrying it, and whether the store could be read. The Search view's category filter is populated from this; browser.category.set / browser.category.clear edit it. Read-only.

Remove a file's category from the browser's library, persisting the store. Not-found when the file carries none: a clearing that clears nothing is a refusal. Reversible: the recorded inverse is browser.category.set with the category the file carried, which control.undo dispatches.

Classify a file in the browser's library: 'category' (a label with a tag's bounds) is filed against the file's canonical path in the tag store's categories table, ONE per file - setting it over an existing one replaces it, and the vocabulary browser.categories lists and the Search view's category filter offer grows with it. The write is reported: a category that cannot be persisted is a refusal, not a silent success. Refused when the file already carries it. Reversible: the recorded inverse is browser.category.set with the previous category (browser.category.clear when there was none), which control.undo dispatches.
Remove a smart collection ('name'). One undo step.
What a smart collection ('name') finds now - browser.query's answer for its stored query, with 'limit', 'offset' and 'probe' as browser.query takes them.

Save a search as a smart collection: 'name' and browser.query's 'text' (a substring or an expression - OR, -word, "phrase", name: path: tag: kind: ext:), 'tags', 'kind', 'root' and 'category'. A collection of the same name is replaced. Kept beside the browser tags in the config directory, not the project; one undo step.
The saved smart collections, each with its query.
The browser's history (most recent last) and where it stands. Session state.
Go back ('step' -1, the default) or forward (+1) - or several steps - in the browser's history: the remembered list is run again and its result answered.

browser.query over the library index - the whole library, without walking it: 'text' (a substring or an expression - OR, -word, "phrase", name: path: tag: kind: ext:), 'tags' (all of them), 'kind', 'category' (the files carrying that one category; empty matches every category), 'limit' and 'offset'. As fresh as the last browser.reindex; the tags and the category are as fresh as the store now.
What the library index holds - entries, files measured, when it was built, the folders, whether a scan is running and how far it is - and where it is kept.

Load the audio file or preset 'path' onto a new track - what Enter does on a browser result: a preset (.xpf) becomes the new instrument track's settings, any other file opens in the instrument that takes its extension (a sample in AudioFileProcessor). 'as' sample_track puts an audio file on a new sample track instead (Shift+Enter). A project or MIDI file is refused: project.open and project.import take those. One undo step removes the track.

The waveform peaks of an audio file: 'buckets' min/max pairs over the interleaved samples, the frames each bucket covers, the file's rate, channels and length, and whether the answer came out of the cache ('cached') or off the disk. The cache is bounded (capacity entries, base_buckets per file) and its hit and miss counts are reported. Read-only: it writes no project state and nothing at all on disk.

Play the audio file 'path' (its first 30 seconds) to hear it - as it is ('match' none, the default), or matched to the song: 'tempo' stretches it to the song's tempo with its pitch kept, 'key' moves it to the song's key ('key' 0..11, else the detected key, else the scale set with scale.set), 'both' does both. The file's tempo and key are the import detection's (half/double tempo is folded). A new preview stops the last. Session audio, not project state.

The mixer channel the browser's previews (a sample, a preset) play into - a cue bus, say, instead of the main mix. The master by default. A preference kept in the config file; with no arguments it reports it.
Stop the browser's preview.

Find files in the browser by name, by tag, or - with 'probe' - by what the audio file itself says it is (sample rate, channels, length, and the embedded title/artist/album/comment/genre tags). Every 'tags' entry must be present (AND). 'category' narrows to the files carrying that one category (browser.category.set assigns it; empty matches every category). Sorted by path, so paging with offset is stable. The walk is bounded by scan_limit entries and the probe by probe_limit files, and a result that hit either bound says truncated: true. 'text' is one substring, or an expression: words ANDed, OR (or |) between groups, -word to exclude, "a phrase", and the fields name: path: tag: kind: ext: (e.g. kind:audio tag:drums -loop OR "bass drum"). Read-only.

Scan the library into its index: every root that exists, one root ('root', an id from browser.roots) or one folder ('path', absolute). With 'features' (the default) each audio file is measured - length, loudness, brightness, noisiness, tempo and key - for browser.similar; a file whose size and date are unchanged keeps the features it had. The scan runs in the background (browser.index_status follows it) unless 'wait', which scans here and measures at most 500 files. A cache in the config directory, not the project: nothing is journalled.

Remember 'source' (a browser source's title: Devices, Search, Presets, Samples, ...) as what the browser shows in view 'context'; the browser switches to it when that view opens. What picking a source in the browser does. A preference in the config file, not the project: not journalled.

The directories the file browser reads - the same tabs the sidebar has: the user's samples, the factory samples, the user and factory presets and projects - with a stable id per root, whether each exists on this machine, and the path of the tag store. Read-only.

Save a 'clip' into the library: a sample clip as the audio it plays (a WAV), a MIDI clip as a MIDI file at the song's tempo. Written to 'dir' (absolute; <user samples>/Clips, which the Samples browser lists, when left out) as 'name' (the clip's name when left out), refused when the file exists unless 'overwrite'; 'tags' are added to it. The library is outside the project: one undo step deletes the file again.

The indexed sounds most like the audio file 'path', closest first ('limit', 10 when left out): each with its distance (0 = the same numbers) and the features it was compared on. The file itself need not be indexed; the others must have been measured (browser.reindex).
The source the browser shows in each view (arrange, mix, edit) - empty when none is remembered. A preference in the config file.

Tag a file in the browser's library. The tag is filed against the file's canonical path in a JSON store in the user's config directory, and the write is reported: a tag that cannot be persisted is a refusal, not a silent success. Refused when the file already carries the tag. Reversible: the recorded inverse is browser.tag.remove, which control.undo dispatches.

Remove a tag from a file in the browser's library, persisting the store. Not-found when the file does not carry the tag: a removal that removes nothing is a refusal. Reversible: the recorded inverse is browser.tag.add, which control.undo dispatches.

The tag vocabulary of the library: every distinct tag with the number of files carrying it, how many files carry at least one tag, the store's own path, and whether the store could be read. Read-only.

A waveform picture (PNG, 'width' x 'height', 160 x 48 when left out) of the audio file 'path', drawn from the peak cache and kept in the config directory (or written to 'out', absolute); 'cached' says it was already there. What the browser's gallery view shows. Writes no project state.

Create a parallel bus channel (Mixer::createBusChannel) and return its new ch-<n> id. A bus never receives instrument output; sends INTO it default to pre-fader. Reversible: one undo step deletes the bus this created.
Every parallel bus channel with its stable ch-<n> id, fader, incoming sends and PDC numbers. Read-only.

Delete a bus channel. Refused for a channel that is not a bus. NOT reversible: the command records the bus's full state but nothing recreates a channel with state, so control.undo refuses, typed, and names the fallback.

Apply a stored chain preset to a target: the target's chain becomes the preset's devices, IN THE PRESET'S ORDER, each one restored from its own state document, so the parameters are the values the chain was captured with. The target's existing devices are removed (the plugin.unload lifetime). A preset naming a device this build cannot load is refused and the target's chain is left untouched. Reversible: one control.undo puts the previous chain back, devices and settings. 'chain' (default 0) applies it to parallel chain n of a channel's rack instead.
Bypass every device of the chain of 'target' (a track or channel; 'chain' n for a rack's parallel chain), or with 'bypass' false switch them all back on. One undo step.
Remove every bypassed device from the chain of 'target' ('chain' n for a rack's parallel chain). One undo step puts them back where they were.

Copy every device of a chain ('target', 'chain') to another ('to', or a list of them; 'to_chain'), in order, with their settings: appended, or with 'replace' in place of the devices there. 'copies' says what each destination got; a device that cannot be made stops the rest ('stopped'). One undo step, however many destinations.

One chain preset in full: its name, its file, its device count and every device in order with the plugin's own identity (the LADSPA file and label, the LV2 URI, or the built-in name), the format, and the size and SHA-256 of the device's state document. The state documents themselves are not returned - they are what chain.apply writes back, and chain.list's hashes are what a caller compares.

Every chain preset in the store: its name, its file, its device count and one summary per device (the plugin, the format and the size and hash of the device's own state document). Pass "name" for one preset in full. The store lives OUTSIDE the project - the user preset tree, chainpresets/ - so the presets are the same ones whichever project is open, which is the point of a preset. Writes nothing.

Receive another channel's audio inside a channel's chain: a sidechain send from 'from' (tapped at 'tap_point', post_fader when left out; an existing one is kept) and a Receiver device at slot 'position' of 'target''s chain (the end when left out) that mixes it in at 'level' (0..2, 1 when left out). The mixer refuses a cycle; PDC aligns the send to the channel's input. 'target' is a mixer channel (a track's own chain has no sidechain input). One undo step removes both.
Delete a chain preset from the store. The preset's own bytes are captured first, so the removal is reversible: one control.undo writes the same file, byte for byte, back to its own path.

Rename a stored chain preset. The name is the key, so a rename onto a name the store already holds is refused, typed, and changes nothing. Reversible through a recorded action checkpoint that renames the file back.

Capture a target's effect chain as a named preset: every device in the chain's own order, each with the state document plugin.state_save writes for it (enabled, wet, autoquit and every parameter). Writes ONE file in the store (chainpresets/<name>.zcp), outside the project, so the preset can be applied to a track in another project, and so project.save/project.open cannot lose it. An existing preset of that name is refused unless "overwrite":true. 'target' is a trk-<n> or ch-<n> id; 'chain' (default 0) captures parallel chain n of a channel's rack instead. Reversible through a recorded action checkpoint that puts the file - or the revision it replaced - back.

Empty the project's chord track, reporting how many chords went. An already-empty track is REFUSED, typed: a clear that would change nothing must not leave an undo step behind. Reversible: one recorded action checkpoint holding the whole <chord-track> element as it was.

What chords a MIDI clip's notes spell. The notes are grouped into slices - by default notes that start at the SAME tick; 'window_ticks' widens that for a strummed or humanised take, measured from each slice's first note so a run of sixteenths cannot chain into one huge slice - and each slice is named from this engine's chord vocabulary. Every slice reports the nearest entry with 'missing' (chord tones the slice does not sound) and 'extra' (tones the chord does not contain), so 'exact' false is visible rather than rounded to a name, and the whole clip's key is reported too. Read-only: nothing is written to the clip or the track (write a detection with chord.detect_to_track).

Detect the chords a MIDI clip's notes spell (the same detection chord.detect reports) and write them onto the project's chord track. By default the track is REPLACED; 'append' adds to what is there. A slice with no name in this engine's vocabulary cannot be a chord-track event and is reported as `skipped` - and if nothing at all could be written the track is left EXACTLY as it was and the call is refused, typed, rather than half-written. Reversible: one recorded action checkpoint.

Make an instrument track FOLLOW the chord track while it plays (chord follow): each note the track starts in the arrangement sounds on the nearest tone (down on a tie) of the chord sounding where it starts - 'mode' chord (the default) - or of that chord's scale - 'mode' scale, the chord where it names no scale - and the clip keeps the keys it was written with (note.follow_chords is the destructive twin). 'mode' off stops it. Where the chord track is silent the notes play as written. Saved with the chord track. Reversible: one recorded action checkpoint; setting the mode a track already has changes nothing and records nothing ('changed' false).

The project's CHORD TRACK: every chord with its position, length, root pitch class, the octave the root sounds in, the root's absolute MIDI key, the chord's name and the key (scale) it was written in, plus the track's own bounds. Read-only. The track is project state saved inside <song> as one <chord-track> element (written only when it holds a chord, so a project that never used one is byte-identical to before), and it is what chord.track_write turns into notes. Chord and scale names come from the piano roll's own vocabulary - see chord.progression_list.

GENERATE a named progression into a MIDI clip as notes. The walk and the key are the pre-existing vocabulary's: each step of the progression is the chord on that SCALE DEGREE, built by stacking the scale's own tones in thirds and named by this engine's chord table (a stack the table cannot name comes back with an empty 'chord' and is still written). 'pattern' is block, arpeggio_up, arpeggio_down or broken; 'step_ticks' is how long each chord lasts (default one 4/4 bar); 'steps' defaults to one pass of the walk. SEEDED AND REPEATABLE: 'variation' (0..1, default 0) opens the draws - each chord's voicing, its position and its velocity - and every draw is a pure function of 'seed' and that chord's own identity, so the same request reproduces the same take note for note and a different seed gives a different one. With 'variation' 0 nothing is drawn and the seed decides nothing. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (MidiClip checkpoint).

What this engine can be asked for: the named PROGRESSIONS the generator walks (each a name and the scale degrees it steps through), the SCALES a key may name, the CHORDS a chord-track event may name, the patterns a generation can lay a chord out with, and the group's bounds. Every one of those vocabularies is the piano roll's own (InstrumentFunctionNoteStacking::ChordTable, the table behind its chord and scale selectors) - this group adds no names of its own. Read-only; with 'name' one progression is reported on its own. With 'scale' (and optional 'root' 0..11 and 'octave') every progression is also SPELLED OUT in that key as `suggestions[]`: each entry's own chords, named by the same vocabulary the generator writes with. That is what the progression panel shows before it writes; nothing is written here.

Remove the chord at an absolute tick from the project's chord track, reporting the event that went. A tick that holds no chord is a typed not_found, never a silent success. Reversible: one recorded action checkpoint, and the recorded inverse names chord.set with the removed event's own arguments.

Write ONE chord into the project's chord track at an absolute tick: the chord's name (a chord of this engine's vocabulary - chord.progression_list lists them), its root pitch class, the octave the root sounds in, and optionally its length. The POSITION is the key: a set at a tick that already holds a chord REPLACES it (the command reports `replaced`), so a track cannot hold two chords at once. 'length' 0 (the default) means HOLD - the chord sounds until the next one, which is what a chord track means. Reversible: one recorded action checkpoint (the track is project state the Song's journal checkpoint does not carry), so one control.undo takes the write back.

Write the CHORD TRACK's own chords into a MIDI clip as notes: every event's chord is voiced from its root and laid out under 'pattern' (block, arpeggio_up, arpeggio_down, broken), each event starting where the track says and sounding for as long as the track says (the distance to the next chord, or 'length' for the last one). 'replace' (default true) clears the clip's notes first and reports how many went; false adds to them. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (MidiClip checkpoint). An empty chord track is refused, typed: there is nothing to write.
Create a clip on a track at a tick position and return its stable clip-<n> id. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).

Find the notes of a monophonic line in an audio clip (a voice, a bass, a lead; YIN pitch tracking - a strong harmonic can read an octave out) and write them, with their loudness as velocity, onto a new instrument track where the audio sits. One undo step removes the track.

Replace the clips of a sample-track region with ONE clip playing their audio: every lane through the composite's gate, with each clip's window, warp, gain and fades - the clips' own audio, not the track's output (the track's devices, fader and pan still apply once, on playback). `start`/`end` (ticks) name the region; neither means every unmuted clip. A clip crossing the region's edge is refused (clip.split it first); muted clips are left in place. The file is stereo float WAV at the engine rate, at `out` or beside the project under a name never reused. Rendered BEFORE anything changes, so a failed render writes nothing; one control.undo restores every source clip and the composite (Track checkpoint).

A MIDI clip's controller lanes - the CC, pitch-bend and aftertouch curves it plays to its instrument: [{lane (cc:<n> | pitchbend | aftertouch), kind, controller, maximum (127, 16383 for pitch bend), points [{tick, value}]}].

Replace one controller lane of a MIDI clip: 'lane' is cc:<0..127>, pitchbend (0..16383, 8192 centre), aftertouch or program (a program change, held from each point to the next); 'points' [{tick (clip time), value}] - linear between points, held before the first and after the last; no points removes the lane. Played to the instrument (and the track's MIDI out) as the clip plays. One undo step (MidiClip checkpoint).

Ramp two overlapping audio clips on one track into each other. mode 'clamp' (default) uses edge fades over the overlap and creates no offset fades. mode 'container' opts into the V-shaped fade for a clip lying inside another; it uses the inner clip's authored fade-in and fade-out lengths and refuses missing or non-fitting ramps. Holding Alt while dropping a clip onto another on the same track invokes that container gesture. outgoing clip gets a fade-out and the incoming clip a fade-in, both exactly as long as their overlap, with the given shape (default equal_power, which sums the pair to unity POWER) - or each side its own: 'out_length' / 'in_length' (ticks) and 'out_shape' / 'in_shape'. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).
Delete a clip from its track. dry_run previews it. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).
Copy a clip on its own track (notes included) and return the copy's id. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).

Write a MIDI clip as a MusicXML score to 'path' (.musicxml or .xml): one part in the song's time signature, quantised to a 64th, notes starting together as chords, long values tied across bar lines. Muted notes are left out. Writes a file; the project is untouched.
A clip's fades, gain envelope and gain as one gain curve, 'points' samples over its length (64): [{tick, gain}] - what the automation editor draws behind the clip. Read only.
A sample clip's gain envelope points.

Replace a sample clip's gain envelope with 'points' ([{tick, gain_db}], tick from the clip's start, -60..+24 dB, at most 32; [] clears it). Between points the gain moves linearly in dB, before the first and after the last it holds; it multiplies the clip's own gain and fades. Saved with the clip. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

Make a clip of a file: a Standard MIDI File becomes one MIDI clip holding all its notes (on an instrument track), an audio file one sample clip (on a sample track), at 'position' ticks. With 'track' the clip goes on that track, which must be of the kind the file needs; without it a NEW track of that kind, named after the file, is created. This is what dropping a file on the arranger runs - from a plug-in editor, the desktop or the browser. Everything that can fail is checked before anything changes: a missing, empty, malformed or unsupported file, a clip that would end past the song, a track of the wrong kind or a locked one is refused and the project is left exactly as it was. Audio read from the temporary folder (a plug-in's drag file, deleted right after) is embedded in the clip; other audio is referenced by path. One undo step removes the clip (and a track it created).

Glue MIDI clips on one track into one: the earliest keeps its id and spans to the last one's end, the others' notes move into it at their song positions and the others are removed (sample clips are joined by clip.consolidate). One undo step (Track checkpoint).

Link clips to a clip so they share its notes, name and colour: an edit to the note list or shared presentation of any member is seen by every member (linked / smart clips). 'clip' is the content source and the group's anchor - if it is already linked, the named clips join ITS group; otherwise a new group is created and 'clip' joins it. The new members ADOPT 'clip'"s notes, name and colour (the group starts in sync), while their own start, length, loop window, fades, gain and take lane stay their own: a link shares content, not placement. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (one Clip checkpoint per member written, merged into one undo step). See docs/LINKED-CLIPS.md.

Read the link groups: every group with its members, the content channel it shares ('notes'), the note count, which member is the reference (the group's first member in arrangement order) and - per member - whether its content still matches the reference (`in_sync`) or has drifted (`divergent`). With 'clip', the report is that clip's group only; without it, every group in the song. Read-only.

Make this linked MIDI clip unique by detaching its instance with an independent copy of its current content. Other members keep their shared content; when only one member remains, its link is dissolved. Reversible through one ProjectJournal checkpoint.

Unlink a clip: it leaves its link group and keeps the content it has, but stops following - and stops being followed by - the other members. This is the operation that detaches (there is no detach-on-edit: an edit to a member propagates). When the group is left with a single member that member's link is dissolved too, so no group of one outlives its last pair; a clip that is not linked is refused, typed. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

Force the group to agree: every other member of 'clip'"s link group is given this clip's content, and the members that had to be rewritten are named in `written`. An edit through the note.* verbs already propagates on its own - this is the REPAIR verb for the edit kinds that do not (a piano-roll gesture the engine's note entry points do not see, a hand-edited project file), and it is what makes a disagreement fixable instead of permanent. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (one Clip checkpoint per member written).
The arrangement's clips: id, name, track, start, length and kind - every one, a 'track''s, or those whose name holds 'name' (any case), at most 'limit' (500).

Move a clip to an absolute tick position. The arranger's modes apply (arrangement.modes): overlap trims or crossfades what it lands on, ripple moves the clips after its old end by the same distance, following automation lanes carry their points. One undo step through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint, or the track's when the move touches other clips).

An audio clip's pre-fades: its fade-in starts 'fade_in' ticks BEFORE the clip and its fade-out ends 'fade_out' ticks AFTER it (0..3840 each, 0 for none; each is one ramp with the clip's own fade, in the same shape), and the clip plays the source audio its trim hides there - lead_ticks reports how much hidden audio the fade-in finds before the in-point. A warped, sped-up or transposed clip has none; a reversed clip or one on a comped track keeps its own span. Saved only when set. One undo step.

Print an audio clip through the devices of a chain - 'from' (trk-<n> / ch-<n>; 'chain' n for a rack's parallel chain) - with their settings: the clip's source is replaced by the processed audio (resampled to the engine's rate), the chain itself is untouched; 'tail' seconds (0..30) of silence are processed too so a reverb or a delay can ring out. One undo step (Clip checkpoint).
Snap the start of each of 'clips' to the nearest 'grid' line (ticks; a bar when left out). One undo step.

Cut out of an audio clip every stretch quieter than 'threshold_db' (-50 when left out) for at least 'min_length' ticks (48, a beat): the clip is split around each and the quiet pieces deleted. One undo step.

Put 'count' copies of a clip (1..64, default 1 - Duplicate) right after it, back to back on its track; answers the copies' ids. With ripple on (arrangement.modes) what follows moves later to make room. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).
Set a clip's length in ticks (the clip becomes manually resized). Linked instances keep independent lengths and loop windows. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).
Select (or clear with an empty id) a clip for roll.get_state and the get_states' selection flags. Control-surface state, not project state.

Set a clip's fade-in and/or fade-out in ticks, with a shape each (linear, exponential, logarithmic, s_curve, equal_power). An omitted argument keeps its current value; fade_in + fade_out must fit inside the clip. 'fade_in_offset' / 'fade_out_offset' (ticks, default 0) start the fade-in that far after the clip's start / end the fade-out that far before its end; set as a pair, the fade-in starting where the fade-out ends. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

A sample clip's formants (Rubber Band): 'keep' holds them where they were while the clip is transposed (a voice stays a voice), 'semitones' (-24..24) shifts them on their own. Both off is the plain pitch shift. The clip's stretch mode becomes Rubber Band; refused, typed, in a build without it. Saved with the clip. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

Set a clip's gain in dB (-60..+24, 0 is unity). The gain multiplies every frame the clip renders, on top of its fades; a clip's own gain is independent of any other clip's. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).
Lock one 'clip' against editing ('locked' false unlocks it), as track.set_locked does for a whole track. Saved with the project; one undo step.

Loop a clip's content: a MIDI clip's notes from the start to 'length' ticks repeat across the whole clip, however long it is drawn (0 stops the loop). An audio clip's audio from 'start' ticks after its in-point (0 when left out) for 'length' ticks repeats the same way once the clip plays past it - kept in source frames, so a tempo change keeps it on the same audio; refused, typed, for a warped, transposed, sped or recording audio clip. Saved with the clip. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

Mute or unmute a clip. The song editor's own clip mute (Ctrl+middle-click and the clip context menu) dispatches this command. A clip of the song arrangement or of the pattern editor is addressed by its stable clip-<n> id. With the chase preference on, unmuting a clip under the playhead starts the notes it was holding. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (the clip's mute BoolModel checkpoint).

Set whether a sample clip renders with its polarity inverted: every frame it plays changes sign, and its drawn waveform mirrors around zero. The SOURCE sample is never modified - the inversion is a non-destructive stage on top of the clip's gain, like its fades - and an old project loads with polarity off. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

Arm (record: true) or disarm an audio clip to receive the input the next time the song plays with recording (the song editor's Record while playing): the take starts where the clip starts, is latency-compensated, and replaces the clip's audio when the transport stops. A MIDI clip is refused - notes are recorded in the piano roll. Reversible through a recorded action step (the flag is not serialized).

Set the point inside a clip, 'ticks' from its start, that lands on the grid when the clip is dragged - a sample's downbeat after a pickup (0 snaps by the start, as before). Saved with the clip. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

Transpose a clip by 'semitones' (-48..+48, 0 resets), non-destructively: a MIDI clip's notes play transposed and keep their keys; a sample clip is pitch-shifted with its timing kept (its stretch mode becomes Rubber Band; refused, typed, in a build without it). Saved with the clip. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

Slice a sample clip's audio into a new SlicerT track - cut 'at' its transients (default) or every beat - with a MIDI clip at the same place that plays each slice where it sat, so the loop sounds as before and can be re-sequenced (at most 69 slices, so every slice has a MIDI key - 'capped' says the rest were left out). One undo step removes the track.

Slip a clip's content inside its own rectangle: the clip's position and its length do not move, and the part of the source that plays at the clip's start becomes 'offset' ticks into it. Slip is the only verb that moves the audio without moving the clip. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

An audio clip's speed, the pitch going with it (a tape): it ramps from 'from' to 'to' percent (25..400; 'to' follows 'from' when only 'from' is given - a fixed varispeed) across the clip, rises from nothing over the first 'fade_in' ticks (a tape start) and falls to nothing over the last 'fade_out' ticks (a tape stop). The clip keeps its length; a slower clip plays less of its audio. Refused for a clip that keeps its pitch while stretched. Saved with the clip. One undo step (Clip checkpoint).

Split a clip at an absolute tick position, leaving the left part in place and returning both ids. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint). ED-021, sample clips only: 'frames' cuts that many engine frames after 'position' (frame-exact - the halves' audio meets at that frame, their clips overlap by under a tick), and 'zero_crossing' (default: arrangement.modes' snap_to_zero_crossings) moves the cut to the nearest zero crossing within 10 ms; the reply then names the source 'frame' cut at. Splitting a linked instance cuts only that instance; both halves stay linked and keep the shared content through their independent windows.
Cut a clip into pieces: 'at' transients (sample clips), beats, bars, markers or positions ('positions', song ticks); cuts outside the clip are ignored. One undo step (track checkpoint).

Scale a clip's content in time by 'factor' (0.125..8; 2 = twice as long): a MIDI clip's note positions and lengths scale with it; a sample clip leads with a source tempo of the project tempo times the factor, so it plays at 1/factor speed (pitch kept when its stretch mode keeps it). The clip's length scales too. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).
Where a sample clip's audio has its hits: [{frame (source), tick (from the clip's start, where it plays now)}] - the onset rule detect.* uses.

Move a clip's start edge to an absolute tick, holding the audio the clip already carried at the same song position: the start, the length and the source offset move together, which is what the song editor's own left-edge drag does. An optional 'end' trims the tail in the same step. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint). ED-021, sample clips only: 'start_frames' / 'end_frames' put an edge that many engine frames after its tick (frame-exact: the clip's window takes the frame, the sub-tick rest its lead), and 'zero_crossing' (default: arrangement.modes' snap_to_zero_crossings) moves each edge to the nearest zero crossing within 10 ms; the reply then adds the window's source frames. Linked instances keep independent position, length and source window.

What this engine's MIDI clock is doing: the master's enabled flag, the port it sends on and whether that port is subscribed to a client destination, the message counters it has emitted and a bounded monitor of the last messages in order; and the slave's enabled flag, its source port, the number of clock messages IGNORED for arriving on another port, whether it follows the measured tempo, whether it is LOCKED, the measured tempo, the drift of the last interval from the window's mean, the drift bound, the tempo error the pulse jitter can produce, the window it measures over, the pulse count and the last song position and time-code values received. Read-only. `mtc` reports "absent": this release generates no MIDI time code (see docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).

Enable or disable the DAW as a MIDI clock MASTER: 24 clock pulses to the quarter note, START/STOP/CONTINUE and a Song Position Pointer on the transport's own edges, emitted from the audio thread through this engine's MIDI output. `port` names the writable client destination to subscribe to (see midi.device_list for the names); an empty one keeps the current subscription. Enabling when the engine has no MIDI client to send through is refused, typed, rather than reported as a success that emits nothing. Reversible: the enabled flag AND the port subscription are restored by control.undo.

Enable or disable the DAW as a MIDI clock SLAVE: follow an incoming clock, measure its tempo over one quarter note of pulses and, when follow_tempo is on, write that tempo to the Song once it has left the dead band. A slave that is enabled with NO clock arriving never locks, writes nothing and does not move the transport - clock.get_state reports locked:false. `source_port` names the readable client port to follow, spelled as midi.device_list spells it (Edit > MIDI Clock > Clock Source offers the same list): clock messages from any OTHER port are ignored and counted in `ignored`, and choosing a different source forgets the measurement so the device moved off cannot keep writing its tempo. An empty source_port follows a clock from wherever it arrives - that is how the choice is CLEARED, while OMITTING the property keeps the current one - and it is the only value a client with one unnamed input (ALSA Raw-MIDI, JACK, OSS, sndio, the dummy) can follow, because those cannot say which of their ports a byte came from. A name longer than the follower can hold is refused (invalid_args), never truncated. `drift_bound_ms` is how far one pulse interval may stray from the window's mean and still count as locked. Reversible for the CONFIGURATION: the tempo a following slave wrote is a trajectory of writes, not one state, and control.undo does not restore it (the transaction names the value). Receiving START/STOP/CONTINUE/SONG POSITION is counted and reported; moving the transport FROM the incoming clock is not in this release (see docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).

The session: mode (idle, hosting, joined), the peers with their roles and connection, the port and the router mapping (method, external address, whether the internet can reach it), the last notice and the undo model. Never includes an invite or key.

Host a peer-to-peer collaboration session (no server): listen on TCP 'port' (default 41740; any free port when that one is taken) with TLS-PSK encryption, and with 'map_port' (default true) ask the router to open it (PCP/NAT-PMP, then UPnP). Needs 'consent': true; a person at the screen is asked as well. 'name' is how peers see you. The router's answer arrives in collab.get_state's host.mapping.

The invite for a 'role' (editor - default; viewer; remote: transport, markers and faders only) as one copyable string carrying the address, port and that role's 128-bit key. 'scope': auto (the router's public address when the mapping worked, else the LAN address), public, lan, or local (127.0.0.1). The invite is a secret: whoever holds it can join as that role.

Join a session with an 'invite' (ZENE1-...). The host's project replaces the open one, then every edit made through a command stays in step: yours go to the host, which applies and streams them to everyone in its order. 'name' is how others see you. Asynchronous: follow collab.get_state's peer.state.
Leave the session; the project stays open here as it was.
Send the host's project again: a host re-sends it to every peer, a peer asks the host for it.
Host only: change connected 'peer' (its id) to 'role' (editor, viewer, remote).
Show the collaboration panel (host, invites, join, who is connected).
Stop hosting: every peer is disconnected and the router mapping removed.

Assign an audio or MIDI clip to a take lane of its own track: the lane tag is a field on the clip, so the take is the clip and its content is never copied or moved. A lane the clip's track does not have is refused, as is a pattern or automation clip. A MIDI take is comped by NOTE: a note plays where the composite selects its clip's lane at the note's start (docs/COMPING.md). Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

Audition one take lane: while it is set, that lane's takes play WHOLE and every other lane of the track is silent - the composite is set aside, not changed. Omit 'lane' (or pass -1) to stop and play the composite again. Monitoring state: not saved and not journalled, so it records no transaction. Takes effect from the next clip a playback pass starts.

Cycle the take a comp segment plays: the segment at 'tick' (the play position when left out) on 'track' switches to the next take lane ('direction' next, the default) or the previous one, wrapping round. One undo step.

One track's comping state: its take lanes (with the ids of their takes), the composite's ordered segments, and what each segment resolves to - the take clip and the source frame its first tick reads. A segment whose lane has no take covering it is reported as 'unresolved', never guessed at. Reads only.

Add a take lane to a track and return its index. The index is the lowest one the track does not use; a lane is never renumbered by a removal (docs/COMPING.md). The lane holds no audio of its own: the takes are the clips tagged with that index, assigned with comp.assign. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).
List take lanes: the named track's, or every track's in song order when no track is given. Each lane reports its index, its name and the ids of the takes assigned to it (comp.assign). Reads only.

Remove a take lane from a track. Any composite segment that named the lane falls back to the track's base lane, because a composite stays gapless over its span; removing the last lane clears the composite. A lane the track does not have is refused, typed, naming the lanes it does have. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).

Move the boundary between two takes of the composite nearest 'tick' to 'to': the take on the growing side carries on in time (the same lane at its own slip). Refused where no take of that lane reaches over the range it would grow into. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).
Set whether every take on this track plays together. This is track-wide and saved with the project. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).

Rebuild the composite: sort it, merge neighbouring segments that are the same lane at a continuous offset, and - when a span is given - clamp the composite to exactly [begin, end) and fill every gap in it with the track's base lane. With no span it normalises what is already there (idempotent on a well-formed composite). The take audio is not touched. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).

Choose which take lane supplies the composite over [begin, end) ticks, slipped 'srcpos' ticks (default 0 = the take at its own place; N pulls N ticks of later take material under the range - an audio track only, refused on a MIDI one). A selection paints over what was there: the range is cut out of every existing segment and the new choice is inserted, so the composite stays ordered and gapless over its span. The take audio is not touched, and nothing is copied. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).

comp.select on several tracks at once - 'tracks', or the edit set of VCA group 'group' (a kit recorded across tracks): lane 'lane' supplies [begin, end) on every one, slipped 'srcpos'. Refused, with nothing changed, when any track cannot take it. One undo step for all of them.

Turn a take recorded across loop wraps into takes: the clip (starting at the loop's start, longer than the loop) is cut at each wrap, every pass goes on its own take lane at the loop's start, and the last pass is comped in (refused past 32 passes). Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).

Choose which pass of a recorded clip group plays. Name any take clip in the group and its lane; the choice stays active through later loop passes until chosen again. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).
Every registered command with its schemas and requires declaration.

Walk the undo history several steps at once: 'steps' negative undoes that many, positive redoes them - control.undo / control.redo run in turn, so an irreversible command stops the walk where it stands ('stopped' says why) and a coalesced run is one step. 'steps' in the reply is how far it went.
The stable-id contract: every id family, its persistence, its form, the document element it lives on, and the current count.
Liveness probe; also reports whether the engine is addressable yet, why not when it is not, and how many render jobs were refused at the bounded queue capacity.
Ask the instance to run its normal shutdown (the reply is sent first). Unsaved changes are discarded unless save is true.

Redo the last undone journal checkpoint. A structural step whose inverse was a one-way action has nothing to redo, and says so: the redo stack is emptied at that point rather than replaying an older step. A redo that re-creates a device which cannot be built again FAILS typed, as control.undo does, instead of answering 'redone'.

Set the window (milliseconds) inside which a run of the same command on the same target is ONE undo step, so a 200-call drag costs one Ctrl+Z. 0 disables grouping entirely, which is the pre-0.3.0 behaviour. Changing the window ends the gesture in flight, so it can never group two gestures retroactively. Does not touch the project.

Set the undo stack's two caps: `steps` (how many undo steps are kept) and/or `bytes` (the serialised size they may occupy). Lowering a cap EVICTS the oldest steps immediately and the result reports how many (`dropped`). If no steps are dropped, one control.undo restores the caps; a change that drops history is recorded as irreversible and control.undo refuses it. Refuses a value outside the declared ceilings rather than clamping it.
Reflect the live menu/toolbar surface: every user-visible action and the command id it declares (SPEC A15).

The transactions recorded for mutating commands (SPEC A16 hook), each with the contract table's class and the serialised size of the record, plus the bounds they are kept within (cap_records/cap_bytes, retained_bytes, evicted, capped).

Undo the last agent command: the engine's own ProjectJournal step it recorded (the same stack the GUI's Ctrl+Z unwinds), or the recorded inverse command when the change is file-level. If the last recorded command has no inverse, this FAILS with the typed 'irreversible' error and names the documented fallback instead of undoing an older command. One call unwinds ONE undo STEP, and one step is one command EXCEPT under the coalescing rule (docs/UNDO-BOUNDS.md): a run of the same command on the same target inside the window - reads in between do not break it - is one step, so the reply's 'undone_commands' is 1 normally and more for a merged span. Set the window to 0 (control.set_undo_coalescing) for strict one-command-per-call granularity. If the journal's top step has no matching transaction record, the reply identifies it as 'unrecorded edit' and includes its step_serial; transaction history is left intact.

Read the engine's own undo stack: its depth and redo depth, the TWO bounds it is kept within (a count cap and a byte budget), the serialised bytes it retains, how many steps a bound has evicted, and the coalescing rule in force (the window, and which commands it groups). Writes nothing.
The product version string and the control protocol version.

Turn LED/feedback output on or off for one MIDI-bound control. With feedback on, every control-change that moves the model is written back to the controller as a control-change on the channel the hardware transmits on, so a motorised fader or a lit ring follows the value the project holds - including after a project load, a MIDI-learn binding or an automation step. Enabling it also moves the control's MIDI port to Duplex mode, because a port that is not output-enabled cannot carry the write; that port mode is serialized in the project, which is why this command records a transaction. 'written' reports whether THIS call's own feedback write was handed to the port's output path, and 'output_events_written' is the port's own count of control-changes that reached the MIDI client - 'written': false with a port that is not output-enabled is the honest answer, not an error. Without a real controller attached nothing consumes the bytes; the count is a write to the client, not a proof that a lamp lit.

Map a parameter to a MIDI controller without learn: the parameter as automation.* addresses it (track + parameter) or by the name controller.surface_state shows ('target'); control-change 'controller' (0..127) on 'channel' (1..16, default 1), listening on every MIDI input; 'soft_takeover' and 'feedback' as controller.soft_takeover / feedback set them. Replaces a mapping the parameter had. One undo step.

Turn soft-takeover on or off for one MIDI-bound control, and/or set the value it waits for. While soft-takeover is on, a hardware control that is bound to a control whose stored value differs from the knob's position is IGNORED: the model does not jump to wherever the knob happened to be. The hardware takes the control over the moment a control-change crosses the stored value (or lands within one MIDI step of it), and only then do that control-change and the ones after it move the model. Without 'target' the value the model holds now is used, which is the reading a user expects: the surface was in some position when the project was saved. 'control' names the model's fullDisplayName() (controller.surface_state lists the names); an empty or absent 'control' means the project's only bound MIDI control. 'captured' reports whether the hardware has already taken over - it is reset by the first movement after enabling, which is what makes a fresh binding wait for the knob.

Read-only: every control in this project that a MIDI controller drives, addressed by the model's fullDisplayName(). Each entry carries the MIDI channel and controller number, the soft-takeover flag and whether the hardware has already taken the control over ('captured'), the value the takeover waits for ('takeover_target'), the LED/feedback flag and the port's two output counters. 'output_events_written' is the count of control-changes this control's port actually handed to the MIDI client's output - the measurement the LED half is proved by, taken at the client boundary in MidiPort (include/MidiPort.h) and not self-reported by the command. This is how an agent reads a surface without a controller in hand.

Apply a saved mapping template to this project: for every binding in it whose target model resolves, create the MIDI controller and the connection that drives that model, and restore the binding's soft-takeover and feedback flags. 'bound' counts the controls the call bound, 'skipped' counts the bindings whose target is not in this project and 'missing' names them - a template saved against another song applies the part that resolves and REPORTS the rest, rather than failing as a whole. A binding whose target is already driven by a MIDI controller is re-bound, which is what makes applying a template a way to move a surface onto a different set of addresses. This creates project state (the model's <connection> element), so the project is marked modified. controller.surface_state reports the resulting surface.

Remove one saved mapping template from this machine. 'removed' is false when no template of that name existed, which is reported rather than treated as an error (the file is the state, and the state asked for - no such file - already holds). No project state is touched: the project's own bindings are unaffected.

Read-only: the mapping templates saved on this machine, by name, sorted, with the directory they live in and - per template - how many bindings it holds, how many of them resolve in the CURRENT project, and the names that do not. A template whose targets do not resolve still lists: it is a saved mapping set, not a claim about the project that is open.

Save the project's current MIDI bindings as a named mapping template - one JSON file in the user preset tree, listed by controller.template_list and re-applied by controller.template_apply. Each binding records the MIDI channel, the controller number, the model's fullDisplayName() and the binding's soft-takeover and feedback flags, so applying a template restores the whole surface and not just the addresses. A template is not a project: it survives closing the project and is what a user with two controllers swaps between. An existing template of the same name is overwritten. 'name' must be one file name - a path separator, a ".." or a leading dot is refused.
Remove a parameter's MIDI mapping (addressed as controller.map takes it). One undo step.

Acknowledge the pending crash report: write the reporter's `offered` sentinel so the report is not offered again on the next start, and KEEP the file so it can still be attached. Refuses when there is no report. Not reversible - no function in this engine removes the sentinel; control.undo names the sentinel to delete by hand.

Disarm the crash reporter's signal handlers (crashreporter::uninstall): the default disposition is restored for exactly the signals install() claimed, so a crash is no longer reported and the process dies as it would without the reporter. Deletes NOTHING - the report, its directory and the session marker survive, and crash.list_reports still names them. Refuses when it is not armed. Reversible through control.undo, which dispatches crash.enable with the directory captured before the call.

Clear the crash reporter's report: delete the report file and the offered sentinel beside it (crashreporter::discardPendingReport). Refuses when there is neither, so a call that would change nothing writes nothing. Not reversible - the report's bytes are gone and nothing writes a report from a caller's bytes; control.undo names the fallback.

Arm the crash reporter's signal handlers (crashreporter::install). With no arguments it re-arms to the report directory the reporter remembers; an explicit `directory` arms that one instead. The result reports `armed` from the kernel's own signal dispositions and `installed` from the module's flag, plus the signal set and the report path. Refuses when it is already armed and when the directory does not exist (install() never creates it). Reversible through control.undo, which dispatches crash.disable.

The crash reporter's state: whether it is installed, where its report directory is, every report it holds (path, existence, size, last-written time), whether a report is still pending an offer, whether the offered sentinel is present, whether a session marker says the previous run exited uncleanly, its two hard bounds, and the upload policy. Read-only, and it answers in every configuration.

Send a crash report somewhere. Refused, always: this build has no upload and no network code of any kind in the reporter (include/CrashReporter.h states it as a design property), so no send is faked. The refusal names the file to attach by hand.

The DAWproject version and convention this build implements, as data: the format's name and version (README.md: "The format is version 1.0 and is stable"; Project.xsd declares version="1.0"), the container's two entry names and its text encoding, the time unit every time value is written in, LMMS' own ticks per quarter note and the exact rule between a tick and a beat, the ZIP method used, the contentType vocabulary and how LMMS' nine track types map onto it, and the STATED LOSSES - everything this module does not carry. A file declaring another MAJOR version is refused rather than read with this build's assumptions.

Write the session as a .dawproject container: a ZIP whose project.xml carries the tracks, their clips and notes, the tempo map and each track's mixer strip, in the published format's own vocabulary at version 1.0. The file is written with STORE entries so every ZIP reader opens it (import reads STORE and DEFLATE). `loss` in the reply reports EXACTLY what the format could not carry from this session. Refuses an existing file unless `overwrite` is true, and refuses a relative path. Writes a file; changes nothing in the session.

Apply a .dawproject container's model to the session: REPLACE the tracks, write the global tempo and time signature, replace the tempo map with the file's two automation timelines and set the mixer strips it carries. One command, one undo: the whole session captured before the import is put back through the project loader's own paths when the stack unwinds. Reads STORE and DEFLATE ZIP entries under a 512 MiB per-entry and 1 GiB total decompressed-size bound. `loss` in the reply reports what the file carried that this build does not apply, and `deviations` lists everything in the container that was not taken as written (a corrupt, CRC-failing, unsupported or oversized entry, a file project.xml references that the container lacks); the import still proceeds when project.xml itself is readable. Refused, typed, when the file cannot be read, when a tempo or metre is outside the engine's own bounds, or when the file needs more tempo-map events than the map holds - a refusal writes nothing.

Read a .dawproject container's model WITHOUT touching the session: the format version the file declares, the application that wrote it, every track with its clips and notes, the tempo and time-signature timelines, the mixer strips, the entries the container carries that this module does not use, and the model's printable digest - what makes a round trip checkable against the FILE and the MODEL rather than a hash. Reads ZIP entries using STORE (method 0) and DEFLATE (method 8) under a 512 MiB per-entry and 1 GiB total decompressed-size bound. `deviations` lists EVERYTHING in the container that was not taken as written - a corrupt or CRC-failing entry, an unsupported compression method or encryption, an oversized entry, a file project.xml references that the container lacks - while the readable entries are still read. A file that is not a ZIP, has no readable project.xml entry, declares another major format version, or carries a value the engine will not accept is a typed refusal that lists the deviations too.

Analyse an audio file the importer can read and report what it implies: the tempo (BPM) over the declared 40..240 BPM band, the FIRST transient (in seconds and frames), and the key as a tonic pitch class plus a scale name from the pre-existing scale vocabulary - each with the detector's own score and the method that produced it. Writes NOTHING: this is the suggestion BACKLOG.md item 10 asks for, and `detect.apply` is the acceptance. Reads at most `max_seconds` (default 60) from the START of the file.

Analyse an audio file and WRITE the result into the project's own fields: the detected tempo becomes a tempo-map event at tick 0 (the map is switched on, and the whole BPM is the map's integer - the exact estimate is reported back beside it), and the detected key is stored in the project's `<detected-key>` field under a scale name the pre-existing vocabulary knows. `tempo` and `key` select the halves (both default to true); a half the analysis found nothing for is REFUSED and NOTHING is written. Both writes are ONE undoable step: control.undo takes the whole detection off.

Read back what the project holds: the detected key (the `<detected-key>` field, when a detection has been applied), the tempo map's own state and what it answers at tick 0, the scale vocabulary a key name can come from, the two detection method names, the bounds - and the accuracy sentence (`method.accuracy_note`), which says plainly that real-world accuracy is unverified and that the confidence numbers are scores, not probabilities.

Whether MIDI Polyphonic Expression input is on, and what that means in this engine: the flag itself, which axes reach PLAYBACK and how (all three do - pitch as a frequency ratio the engine applies to the note itself, and pressure and timbre as MIDI channel pressure and CC74 sent to the instrument on the channel the note's own note-on took, which for a note captured from an MPE controller is its member channel; the two MIDI axes need an instrument that consumes them - a hosted instrument or a MIDI output port - because the built-in synthesisers are driven by frequency and volume and never see MIDI), how a note stores its capture (the optional mpepitch / mpepressure / mpetimbre attributes), the channel count and master channel the model assumes, the default bend range and the MPE+ cap on notes per channel. Read-only. 'per_stream_settings_reachable' is false and the result says why: the master channel and bend range live on a MIDI input stream's own MpeExpression, which no object the control surface holds owns.

Turn MIDI Polyphonic Expression INPUT on or off. While it is on, a bend / channel pressure / CC74 arriving on a note's own MPE member channel is that note's expression and is consumed instead of bending the whole instrument; while it is off the input path is exactly what it was before MPE existed (the engine's own flag is deliberately NOT serialized, so a project never changes meaning because of it). All three axes reach playback: pitch as a frequency ratio, pressure and timbre as MIDI channel pressure / CC74 on the note's own channel - which a hosted instrument or a MIDI output port consumes, and no built-in synthesiser does. Switching it off does NOT clear what is already stored on the notes: note.expression_get still reads it, and note.expression_clear is the verb that removes it. Reversible: a recorded action step restores the previous flag, so control.undo and Ctrl+Z are one history.

Every device chain with its fx-<n> instances, each one's parameter values and, on an instrument track, its 'inst' entry with the instrument's parameters. With 'target' it reads exactly that target, an empty chain included; without it, every track and mixer channel that carries at least one device.

Read the render settings that outlive one OutputSettings: whether the next export dithers, which sample-rate-conversion quality it resamples with, and whether it writes an EBU R128 loudness report beside its output.
