The patcher node graph of a target's effect chain: every node with the role a patch addresses it by ("input", "effect:<index>"), its type, its ports, its own parameters and whether it is prepared; the edges in node ids and in roles; the cached topological order the audio thread walks; the output node; and whether the wiring is the DERIVED one (linear, from the effect list) or an AUTHORED patch. Read-only. `editable` reports whether an edit can land at all, with the reason when it cannot.

Re-wire a target's effect chain: 'edges' is the whole wiring ({from, to, from_port, to_port} objects whose ends are "input" or "effect:<index>"), 'output' is the node the host block leaves through (the last effect by default), and an empty or absent edge list restores the DERIVED wiring. The new graph is built off the audio thread and published under the audio engine's model-change guard, so the edit is never concurrent with the render (include/RoutingGraph.h's threading contract) and it survives the next plugin.load - the derived rebuild re-applies it. Refused, typed, with nothing written, when the chain does not render through its graph (see patcher.get_state's `editable`), when an edge would make a cycle, or when the output cannot be reached from the input. Reversible: the previous wiring, derived or authored, is restored by control.undo.

Plugin delay compensation as the mixer publishes it: the total latency to the master output, every channel's alignment point and the latency its own chain adds, the compensation applied at every send, and whether sidechain routing exists. Read-only.

Q050-339: the manual delay of 'target' - an audio track or an instrument track (trk-<n>), or a mixer channel (ch-<n>, not the master) - as 'offset_samples', a whole number of samples at the engine's rate (-8192..8192): positive plays it later, negative earlier. It is added to the automatic delay compensation, so every other path stays aligned (pdc.report shows the result). A track's offset moves its audio output (not a hosted instrument's extra routed output buses); an instrument track's note delay (track.set_delay) is a separate setting. With only 'target' it reports; the answer adds 'offset_ms' and 'kind' (track or channel). Saved with the track or channel; one undo step.

Compare two settings of one device: 'store' puts the current settings in 'slot' (a or b), 'recall' puts a stored slot's settings on the device, 'toggle' keeps the current settings in the slot heard now and recalls the other (the first toggle copies them, so A and B start equal), 'get' answers which slot is heard and which are stored. The slots last the session, not the project; a recall or toggle is one undo step.
Mix the two settings plugin.ab stored for an effect: every parameter set 'amount' of the way from slot A's value to slot B's (0..1, 0.5 when left out). One undo step.

Switch a device instance off or on. This drives the same enabled control the rack's On/Off LED drives, so a bypassed device reports processing=false in dsp.get_state. Reversible through the ProjectJournal.

Copy one device ('plugin', fx-<n> on 'target' - with 'chain' for a rack chain) to another chain: 'to' (trk-<n> / ch-<n>, or a list of them; 'to_chain' for a rack chain), at 'position' (0 = first; appended when left out), with its settings. 'plugins' answers the copies' fx-<n>, 'copies' each destination's; a copy that cannot be made stops the rest ('stopped'). One undo step, however many destinations.

Hear only what an effect changes ('plugin' fx-<n> on 'target'): its output minus its input - silence while it changes nothing, the part a compressor takes away (inverted), the harmonics a saturator adds. 'on' switches it, toggling when left out. A monitor switch, like the listen bus: not saved, no undo step.
Close a device's own editor window, if it has one open. 'was_open' says whether there was one; closing a closed editor is not an error. Needs a display; nothing is saved or journalled.

Open a device's OWN editor - the plug-in's interface, not the host's generic knob view (which stays) - in a window of its own. 'target' is the track or channel (trk-<n>/ch-<n>) and 'plugin' the device on it (fx-<n>, or 'inst' for a track's instrument), as plugin.param_set names them. VST3 plug-ins with an editor view and CLAP plug-ins whose gui embeds in X11 open; a plug-in with no editor, or one that can only float, refuses with the reason. An editor already open is brought forward. Needs a display; interface state, not project state: nothing is saved or journalled.

Fold an effect's card on the Device panel to its header ('folded' true), or open it again; toggles when 'folded' is left out. View only - the sound does not change. Saved with the device; one undo step.

The chunking contract both plugin host paths keep, and what this instance's audio path has actually been asked for: per host, the process() calls that reached a loaded plug-in, the frames they asked for, the plug-in calls they were turned into, the requests that needed more than one chunk and the frames beyond the prepared block they carried, the largest request and the block size the last one was prepared with. 'chunks' > 'requests' with a non-zero 'frames_beyond_prepared_block' is a request that was chunked instead of truncated or over-run. Counters are process-wide and never reset; read-only.

The note path the CLAP host keeps, and what this instance has actually carried: the note input ports (clap.note-ports) and the audio layout of the CLAP plug-in loaded last, plus the note events the MIDI route pushed, the ones the bounded queue (or a missing note port) refused, the ones put into a plug-in's input event list and the note-ONs among them. A plug-in with no note input port refuses every note and counts it here rather than hiding it. Read-only.

Load an impulse response - an audio file (WAV, FLAC, OGG...), stereo or mono, up to 5 seconds - into a Convolution Reverb ('plugin' fx-<n> on 'target'); it is resampled to the engine's rate and saved with the device. One undo step puts the previous response back.

Every device this build can load: built-in effect and instrument modules plus the devices of the shipped hosting formats (LADSPA, LV2, VST3 and CLAP), each with a dev-<n> id that is deterministic for the binary. dev-<n> is a catalogue index, not a persisted project id, and 'loadable' says whether plugin.load accepts the entry. Each entry carries 'vendor' - who made it, as its own format reports it ("Zene Studio" for a built-in, the LADSPA maker, the LV2 author, the VST3 or CLAP factory's vendor; empty when the format reports none, which the device picker reads as "Not reported"). Format order is built-in, then LADSPA, then LV2, then VST3, then CLAP, so adding a host does not renumber the ids of the formats that were already there.

Load a device by its dev-<n> id: an effect onto a track's device chain or a mixer channel's insert chain, an instrument onto an instrument track. Returns the new instance id (fx-<n>, or inst for an instrument). Headless-safe: it declares no 'requires' at all, because no editor is created here - neither a built-in plugin view nor an LV2 UI. An LV2 device whose bundle ships a GUI loads and is fully parametrisable through plugin.param_get / plugin.param_set on a display-less instance. Optional for an effect: `chain` (default 0) puts it on parallel chain n of a mixer channel's rack (rack.add_chain), and `position` (0 = first) inserts it at that slot instead of appending; the reply's `index` is the slot it landed in.

Add a MIDI part to an instrument track: notes in the key range (0..127) and velocity range (0..200, the note volume) are sent to the instrument on 'midi_channel' (1..16). Channel-wide messages (pitch bend, controllers) then go to every part's channel. Saved with the track. Reversible through the ProjectJournal.
Drop a MIDI part (part-<n>) from an instrument track; a note sounding on its channel still ends there. Reversible through the ProjectJournal.

Change a MIDI part (part-<n>) of an instrument track in place: its 'midi_channel' (1..16), its key range (0..127) and its velocity range (0..200). A field left out keeps its value, and the part keeps its place in the first-match order. Saved with the track. Reversible through the ProjectJournal.

List an instrument track's MIDI parts: key and velocity zones that each send their notes on one MIDI channel (1..16), so one track plays several parts of a multitimbral plug-in. First match wins; a note no part claims keeps the track's own channel. Read-only.

Move one device ('plugin', fx-<n> on 'target' - with 'chain' for a rack chain) to slot 'position' of its own chain (0 = first; clamped to the last slot). 'from' answers where it was. One undo step; a device already at that slot changes nothing.

Open a file in the instrument a track already carries - what the instrument window's Open button does: an .sfz in the SFZ Player, a sample in the Audio File Processor. The instrument must be the one that opens the file's extension (browser.load puts a file on a NEW track instead). A file the instrument cannot load is refused and the instrument keeps what it had. One control.undo step restores the previous file and settings.

An effect's compatibility and editor options: 'generic_editor' opens the host's generic controls instead of the plug-in's own window; 'keep_running' never puts it to sleep on silence; 'latency_override' is the latency in frames delay compensation uses instead of what it reports (-1: its own); 'editor_scale' is the zoom its own window opens at (0.5..3, for plug-ins that can scale). With none given it reports them (and its aliases and fold). Saved with the device; one undo step.
The plug-ins sorted with plugin.organise - each with its key, favourite, hidden, folder and name - and the folders in use; 'folder' lists one folder's.

Sort a plug-in in the pickers: 'favourite' (listed under Favourites), 'hidden' (left out unless hidden entries are shown) and 'folder' (a folder of your own; empty takes it out). Name it by 'device' (plugin.list's dev-<n>) or by its 'key' (plugin.organisation answers keys). A field left out keeps its value. Kept in the config file, not the project; one undo step.

Route one of an instrument's extra output buses (1..n) to a mixer channel ('channel': ch-<n>), or un-route it ('channel' empty). The bus bypasses the track's volume, pan and effects, follows the track's mute and is aligned by the channel's latency compensation. A VST3 aux bus is activated (with every bus before it) when first routed. Saved with the project. Reversible through the ProjectJournal.

List an instrument track's output buses: bus 0 is the instrument's main output (it reaches the track as always), every other bus - a drum sampler's separate outputs, a multitimbral synth's part outputs - plays into the mixer channel it is routed to ('channel'), or nowhere. 'active' is false for a VST3 aux bus the plug-in keeps off until it is routed. Read-only.

Create one mixer channel per extra output bus of an instrument that is not routed yet, named after the track and the bus, and route the bus to it - the multi-output setup in one step. 'created' lists each bus and its new ch-<n>. One undo step removes the channels again.
Read one device parameter by 'name' or by 'index'. 'plugin' is an fx-<n> instance id or 'inst' for the target track's instrument. The range reported is the engine's own model range.

Give a parameter of an effect ('plugin' fx-<n> on 'target'; the parameter by 'name' or 'index') a name of your own, 'alias' - shown on the device's card; an empty alias puts the parameter's own name back. The parameter keeps its own name as its address (macros, modulators, plugin.param_*). Saved with the device; one undo step.

The parameters whose name - or the alias a user gave it - holds 'query' (any case), on 'target' (trk-<n> / ch-<n>: its instrument, its devices and, for a channel, its rack's chains) or, without one, on every track and channel: target, plugin (fx-<n> or inst), device, index, name, alias. At most 200.

Set one device parameter by 'name' or by 'index' with the engine's own range enforcement: a value outside the model's min..max is refused with invalid_args rather than silently clamped. Reversible through the ProjectJournal.

The folders each hosted format (vst3, clap, lv2) scans: 'dirs' - your own, searched first - 'defaults' - the format's usual places - and 'searched', the folders a scan reads now (each once, only those that exist). 'applies' says when a change is read: rescan (plugin.rescan) or next_start (LV2).

Replace your own folders for one format ('format' vst3 / clap / lv2, 'dirs' a list of paths; empty clears them). Kept in the config file, not the project; one undo step. Run plugin.rescan to read them (LV2: from the next start).

The format the pickers list when a plug-in is installed in several: clap, vst3, lv2 or ladspa (empty lists every format). The plug-in's other formats are left out of the lists, shown again with the hidden entries. With no arguments it reports it. Kept in the config file; one undo step.

The preset files (*.xpf) available to a device: the user preset directory and the factory preset directory, the same two the product's browser reads. An effect's directory is the device's own name (its LADSPA label when hosted); an instrument's is its product preset folder.
Load a preset (*.xpf) into a device: the user preset directory is searched first, then the factory one. A document written for a different device is refused.
Delete one of the device's user presets ('name'); factory presets are read-only. One undo step writes the file back.
Rename one of the device's user presets from 'name' to 'new_name' (refused when that name is taken). One undo step.

Save the current device state as a preset (*.xpf) in the product's user preset directory. An instrument writes the instrument-track preset document the browser loads; an effect writes the device's own state document, because this build has no separate effect-preset format. An existing preset of the same name is refused unless "overwrite":true.

New settings for a device ('plugin' fx-<n> or inst on 'target'): every parameter moves towards a random value inside its own range by 'amount' (0..1, 0.5 when left out; 1 is fully random). The device's on/off switch, mix and decay stay. 'seed' repeats a result. One undo step.

Record what passes a Recorder insert ('plugin' fx-<n> on 'target') to a stereo 24-bit WAV take - 'file', or a new file in the user's Recordings folder - or stop the take ('on' false; it toggles when left out). The sound passes unchanged. It writes the file and nothing else: no undo step. Answers the take, the frames written and any dropped.
Put a Recorder's last take on a new audio track at 'position' (ticks, 0 when left out). One undo step removes the track.

Put another device ('device', plugin.list's dev-<n>) in the place of a device ('plugin', fx-<n> on 'target' - 'chain' for a rack chain): the same slot of the same chain. One undo step brings the old one back with its settings.

Run the plugin scan the factory already has (PluginFactory::discoverPlugins, the slot the GUI never re-invokes): re-read the cache, drop quarantined files, serve what the cache can still be trusted for, load what changed, and rewrite the cache. This is what APPLIES a quarantine edit. Reports the scan's own numbers before and after. Not reversible: the previous fingerprint record of a file the scan replaced is not restorable by any command.

The plugin scan cache and its quarantine list: the cache file and whether it is persistent and dirty, how many records it holds, the quarantine entries with their reasons and whether the files are still there, and the last scan's own report (files found, quarantined, served from cache, known-bad skipped, scanned, descriptors). Read-only.

Every record the scan cache remembers, sorted by path: the file's fingerprint (path, size, mtime), its status (has-descriptor / not-a-plugin / load-failed) and, for a plugin, the descriptor metadata the scan resolved. Read-only; this is the cache's contents, where scan_cache_get_state only reports how many there are.

What the scan cache remembers about one plugin file: whether a record exists for it, whether that record would still be SERVED (the file's size and mtime must both still match - `cached`), whether it is stale (a record exists and no longer matches - `stale`), and whether the quarantine list hides it. Read-only.

Quarantine a plugin file: add it to the scan cache's skip list, with a reason, and write the cache file. A quarantined file is not loaded and not offered to the device catalogue on the next scan (plugin.rescan applies it). ONE entry per path: adding a path that is already listed is refused rather than silently ignored. Reversible - control.undo dispatches the recorded plugin.scan_cache_quarantine_remove.

Un-quarantine a plugin file: drop it from the scan cache's skip list, write the cache file, and report the reason the entry carried. The next scan loads the file again. Reversible - control.undo dispatches the recorded plugin.scan_cache_quarantine_add WITH the reason captured before the removal (a path-only re-add would lose it).

Stop the background plug-in rescan at its next file boundary and keep the previous catalogue: plugin.scan_status then reports outcome cancelled with what the run had finished, and the records it measured stay cached for the next run. Refused when the last run already ended, not found when no run ever started. The project is not touched.

Start a background plug-in rescan: the same scan plugin.rescan runs, one file per event-loop turn, so the window stays usable - plugin.list keeps serving the previous catalogue until the run commits. Follow it with plugin.scan_status, stop it with plugin.scan_cancel; the task list (task.list) shows it with its progress and Cancel. 'pace_ms' (0..1000, default 0) is the delay between two files, so a progress display or a test can watch the run. Not reversible: a finished run re-measures the files and refreshes the cache, like plugin.rescan.

The background plug-in rescan's progress: whether a run is active, its outcome (never, running, done, cancelled), done/total files and the 0..1 progress, the file being scanned, one entry per finished file (path, status, name, error) in scan order, the run's task.list row and the catalogue_count plugin.list still serves. total_files is 0 until the run's first turn plans the files. Read-only.
Restore a device's state from a file written by plugin.state_save. A document written for a different device is refused, so a state file cannot be pushed into the wrong plugin.

Write a device's state to a file path. An effect writes this fork's zenepluginstate document; an instrument ('inst') writes the product's own instrument-track preset document, the one the browser loads. An existing file is refused unless "overwrite":true, so a save cannot silently destroy a state file.

Remove a device instance (fx-<n>) from a track's chain or a mixer channel. When its state fits the capture cap and the undo stack is addressable, one control.undo re-instantiates the same plugin at the same index with its settings restored. If state exceeds the cap, 'state_xml' is empty and 'state_truncated' is true; its settings cannot be manually restored from that snapshot. When state fits the cap but no inverse is recorded, the transaction's 'before' snapshot contains usable XML for a manual rebuild.
A device's audio-ports model: the input and output pin matrices, their channel counts and names, and the engine's own used-channel caches. Read-only.

Set one pin of a device's audio-ports matrix (the pin connector's own write, AudioPortsModel::Matrix::setPin). Reversible: control.undo re-dispatches this command with the value the pin held before the write.
Take alternative 'name' off the list (its file stays on disk). One undo step. Refused for the alternative the session is: switch away from it first.

Keep the session as it is now as alternative 'name' of this project: written to <project>-alternatives/<name>.mmp beside the main file and listed in the project (the project must have been saved). Saving under an existing name replaces that alternative's file. One undo step takes it off the list (the file stays).

Switch to alternative 'name' ('main' for the main file): the session is saved to its own file first (unless 'save_current' is false), then the other is opened - as project.open, so this is not undoable; switch back instead. The list of alternatives is carried across.
The project's alternatives (name, file, whether it exists) and which one the session is ('main' for the main file).

Render two project files (through the built binary, as child processes) and report which bars of which track differ, with the RMS and peak difference per run of bars. This is the audible answer to `diff`: it names a bar and a track, not a note. Long-running: it renders both projects, track by track. differ=false means the renders matched bar for bar.

Make a project portable: copy every file the project file references from outside its own folder into `dir` (default "media") beside it, and point each reference at its copy as a project-relative `local:` path, so the folder can be moved or shared whole. A copy whose content matches a file already there is reused; a name held by a different file gets ` (2)`. Missing media is reported, not copied. Reversible: one control.undo puts the project file's previous bytes back (the copies stay on disk).

Re-present the musical conflicts a project file carries: the marker comments the mmpz-git merge driver left behind, read back without re-running the merge. Each conflict names the track, the pattern, the note and the bar, and what each side did. Reads one file and writes nothing; conflict_count 0 means the file is not conflicted.

Copy 'tracks' (trk-<n> ids) - device, effects, clips and automation - to the system clipboard, for project.paste_tracks in another open project (another instance) or in this one. Writes the clipboard, not the project.

Semantic, XML-aware diff of two LMMS project files: which elements were added, removed, changed or moved, named by their musical path. Reads both files and writes nothing. This is the diff the repository configures for .mmpz, so `git diff` and this verb show the same operation list.

Write the session's notes as a Standard MIDI File (the midiexport filter, 480 ppq: track 0 is the tempo-map conductor track - the same events as interchange.smf_export - then one track per instrument with its name, program change, MIDI channel and notes). File > Export MIDI dispatches this after its file dialog. A missing `.mid` suffix is appended. The export is written to a temporary file and only replaces an existing file once the new output is proven to exist, so a failed export never reports a stale file as a fresh one (and never destroys the previous one). The session is not modified.
Project file, modified flag, tempo and track count.

Write a folder ('dir', absolute) someone else can open: a copy of the session, every file it uses copied into media/ beside it (the copy names them), and HANDOFF.json - application version, tempo, time signature, length, the devices to install first, the media and any that could not be found. The session and its own file are untouched (nothing to undo; delete the folder).

The same reference list as project.missing_assets, plus a sha256 and a size per reference that is on disk - the identity of the media, so 'the same sample, moved' is distinguishable from 'a different sample with the same name' before anything is rewritten. Also returns one digest over the whole reference set, so two projects that reference byte-identical media compare equal whatever the files are named. Reads only; a reference over the per-file cap (1 GiB) is reported unhashed rather than quietly skipped.

Import a foreign file INTO the session through the import filters this build carries (a Standard MIDI File's notes, a Hydrogen song): the tracks it yields are added beside the existing ones. File > Import dispatches this. Refused, typed, when no filter takes the file - with no dialog, unlike the menu's own failure box. Not undoable: the filters write with the project journal paused.

Tracks from another project ('path', a .mmp or .mmpz): with 'list' it answers that project's song tracks (index, name, type); otherwise it copies the ones in 'tracks' (indices; every one when left out) into this project - device, effects, clips and automation - each keeping its mixer channel: the channel of the same name in this project, or a new one made with the source channel's name, colour, volume, pan and hardware routing (direct out, cue sends, insert send and return); 'created_channels' lists the new ones. A track on the master stays on it. One undo step removes the tracks and the channels made for them.
The tracks and clips locked against editing.

Remove selected files from a project's managed media folder, but only the ones that are STILL unused: called with the paths a project.media_usage preview listed, it rescans the project document and refuses every file a reference now names, every missing or external path, and every symbolic link. 'dir' names the same managed folder the preview listed (default "media"). 'dry_run' reports exactly what would be removed and writes nothing; without it each selected file is deleted. A real removal also requires 'confirm': true - pass it only after showing the paths to a human and getting their authorization. IRREVERSIBLE: a deleted media file cannot be restored by control.undo, so preview first and keep a backup if the file matters. Refuses while the open project is the named one and has unsaved changes, because the saved-file scan would not see them.

The Project Media inventory of a saved project file: one row per file the project references, with a usage count that adds every clip and every supported instrument reference (repeated references to the same file add up), and one row for each file in the project's managed 'media' folder that nothing references. Missing references, unresolved paths and files referenced outside the folder are reported as distinct states and are never cleanup candidates. Reads the project FILE; nothing is written. 'dir' names the managed folder (default "media").

Three-way (base, ours, theirs) merge of LMMS project files through the mmpz-git merge driver. Operates on FILES, not the running session: the merged document is written to the 'ours' path (which is what git expects of a merge driver). 'conflicts' is 0 for a clean merge and the number of musical conflicts otherwise; a conflicted file is marked in place with comments a human resolves and `project.conflicts` re-prints. Exit 2 from the driver (a merge it refuses to write) is an error here, never a silent success.

The project's metadata: 'title', 'artist', 'album', 'genre', 'year', 'composer', 'copyright' and 'comment' (text; an empty one clears the field). A field left out keeps its value; with no arguments it reports them. Saved with the project; one undo step.

Every file a project file references - sample clips, AudioFileProcessor and SF2 instruments, session-view audio slots - and which of those references have nothing on disk at them. Reads the project FILE, so it needs no session and answers for a project that cannot be loaded; nothing is written. The list is empty for an intact project. Sample paths are resolved the way the engine resolves them, with one stated difference: 'local:' and an unresolvable legacy relative path resolve against the project file's own directory rather than the open project's. Copying the media into a portable bundle is NOT this verb (Bar 3).

Replace the session with a new project: the user's default template (or the factory one), or `template` - an absolute path to an .mpt - when given. File > New and the toolbar's new-project buttons dispatch this. The previous session is gone (unsaved edits included), exactly as project.open replaces it. `file` is empty afterwards: a new project has no file until it is saved.

Replace the session with a new document of 'type' (production, mastering or live), from that type's template: the user's own <template dir>/<type>.mpt when there is one; otherwise production is the default template (as project.new), mastering a 'Mix' and a muted 'Reference' sample track with EQ, multiband, compressor and analyser on the master, and live two instruments and three sample tracks. The interface opens the type's view and shows the type in the title. Not undoable, as project.new; unsaved edits are gone.
Load a project file into this running instance.

Paste the tracks project.copy_tracks put on the clipboard into this project, each keeping its mixer channel: the channel of the same name in this project, or a new one made with the source channel's name, colour, volume, pan and hardware routing (direct out, cue sends, insert send and return); 'created_channels' lists the new ones. A track on the master stays on it. Tracks get ids of their own. One undo step removes the tracks and the channels made for them.
The recently opened projects other than the session's own file, most recent first (index, path, name, whether it still exists) - what project.switch picks from.

Point the references of a project file whose value is 'from' - as stored, or resolved to a path - at the file 'to', so the project finds its media again. 'from' is a value project.missing_assets reported; pass 'expect_sha256' to refuse unless the file really is that media (the hash project.hash_assets reported). dry_run previews the change and writes nothing. The document is re-serialised with the product's own serialiser and no other attribute, element or the root's name is touched. Reversible: one recorded action checkpoint holds the previous bytes of the project file, so one control.undo restores it byte for byte. The media is not copied anywhere - the portable-bundle half is Bar 3 and is not this verb.

Restore a retained revision of a project file OVER the live file (policy 'keep-3': revision 0 is the revision the last save replaced). The live file is rotated in first, so the restore is itself recoverable. The session in memory is NOT reloaded: call project.open afterwards to work on the restored bytes.

Save the session. With no path, saves over the project's own file. Before the write, the file being replaced is rotated into the named 'keep-3' revision set (<file>.rev0..rev2, each capped at 8 MiB), so the previous revision is recoverable through project.restore_revision - and control.undo dispatches exactly that for the save it recorded. Q050-007: `format` "v2" saves the project as a v2 CONTAINER (a .mmpz ZIP of one entry per section): a LARGER file than the legacy single-blob .mmpz, which builds older than this one cannot open (`format_note` says so). Without `format` the legacy .mmpz is written unless the setting app/savecontainerv2 is "1" or the project was opened from a container; "legacy" forces the old blob. project.open tells both by content.

Write the session as the user's DEFAULT TEMPLATE (<user template dir>/default.mpt) - what every later project.new starts from. File > Save as default template dispatches this after asking before an overwrite. The session itself is unchanged; an existing default template is REPLACED (`replaced` says so), and one control.undo restores the template file and any backup the save replaced. 0.5.0 L11 (WF-027): with 'name' it writes a NAMED template (<user template dir>/<name>.mpt) instead, which the start hub lists and project.new opens.

Save the session as the NEXT VERSION of its file - <name>-01.mmp, -02, ... the first free one - and make that the project's file; the previous version stays on disk untouched. File > Save as New Version dispatches this. Refused while the session has no file yet (save it once with project.save first), and refused when the version number in the file's name cannot be advanced (the widest version number, or a suffix that is not a number). Needs no interface.

Choose whether THIS project saves its undo history with it (WF-033): 'on' or 'off' overrides the global default (setting undohistory/persist, off unless changed), 'default' follows it. Saved with the project. The newest undo steps (undohistory/steps, 20) are written by project.save and the interface's Save as compressed whole-project snapshots under a cap (undohistory/capmb, 64 MB); steps made before it was turned on cannot be saved.

The project's settings in one place - what the Project Settings dialog shows: 'tempo' (BPM), 'numerator' / 'denominator' (the time signature), 'master_volume' (0..200 %), 'master_pitch' (-12..12 semitones), 'pan_law' (as mixer.options takes it) and 'document_type' (production, mastering or live - the view the interface opens the project in). A field left out keeps its value; with no arguments it reports them. Saved with the project; one undo step.

Place another project ('path', a .mmp or .mmpz) in this one: it is rendered (the CLI render, waiting for it) and its audio put on a new track at 'at' (ticks, 0 when left out), linked to the file so it can be rendered again (project.subproject_refresh); edit it by opening its file. A project that contains this one, directly or through its own subprojects, is refused. One undo step removes the track and the link.
Render subproject 'track' again from its file into a new audio file and point the track's clips at it. One undo step points them back.
This project's subprojects: each track, its project file, the audio it plays, when that was rendered and whether the file changed since ('stale').

Switch to another project: 'path', or 'index' into project.recent (0, the default, is the most recent other one - so repeating it toggles between two projects). The session is saved first when it changed (unless 'save_current' is false; an untitled session with changes is refused rather than lost). With 'keep_as_reference' the project left behind stays open as the reference to copy from (reference.*); if it cannot be opened, the switch completes and returns 'reference_error'. Opens as project.open does, so it is not undoable; switch back instead.

Whether this project saves its undo history with it (WF-033): the project's own setting (on / off / default), the global default and caps (settings undohistory/persist, undohistory/steps, undohistory/capmb), what a save would keep NOW (saveable_steps, saveable_bytes, oversize), and what the last save and load did.
Append an empty parallel chain to a channel's rack and return its index (chain-<n>). Reversible through the ProjectJournal (the recorded undo step removes the chain this command created).
One mixer channel's rack: every chain with its device count, the chain selector, and every macro and key/velocity zone with its targets. 'channel' is a ch-<n> id.

Layer another instrument (an instrument dev-<n>) on an instrument track. It plays into the track's mixer channel, follows the track's volume, pan and mute, and gets a whole-keyboard zone (rack.layer_zone_add / layer_zone_remove narrow it). Its parameters are reached with plugin.param_get / param_set as plugin 'layer-<n>'. Saved with the track. Reversible through the ProjectJournal.
Remove a layer (layer-<n>, n >= 1) from an instrument track's layer rack; its zones go with it and the later layers move down one. Reversible through the ProjectJournal.

Set a layer's mix in an instrument track's layer rack ('layer' layer-<n>; layer-0 is the track's own instrument): 'muted' silences it; while any layer is 'solo', only the soloed layers sound; 'level' (0..2, 1 is unity) is a gain on top of the track's volume - layer-0 has none (its level is the track's volume). A field left out keeps its value. Applied at once, to the notes already sounding too. Saved with the track. Reversible through the ProjectJournal.

Add a key/velocity zone to an instrument track's layer rack: notes in the key range (0..127) and velocity range (0..200) play on 'layer' (layer-<n>; layer-0 is the track's own instrument, which plays every note until it has a zone of its own). Reversible through the ProjectJournal.
Drop a zone (zone-<n>) from an instrument track's layer rack. A layer left with no zone plays no note. Reversible through the ProjectJournal.

Read an instrument track's layer rack: layer-0 is the track's own instrument, layer-1.. the instruments layered on it, and the key/velocity zones that pick which layers a note plays on (every layer a matching zone names sounds - a layer rack stacks). Each layer reports its mix (muted, solo, level - rack.layer_set). Read-only.

Add a macro to a channel's rack: a named scalar (0..1) that drives parameters bound with rack.macro_target_add. Returns its macro-<n> id. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (an action checkpoint removes the macro this command created).
Drop a macro from a channel's rack, targets included. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (the recorded undo step re-inserts the captured macro at its index).

Set a macro's value (0..1) and drive every bound parameter through its own window in one step. Parameters whose device or name no longer exists are skipped and counted ('skipped'), never guessed at. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (one action checkpoint restores the macro and every parameter it wrote).

Set two macros of a channel's rack at once - the XY pad: 'x_macro' to 'x_value' and 'y_macro' to 'y_value' (0..1 each, two different macro-<n>), each driving its bound parameters as rack.macro_set does. Both macros are checked before either is written, so the pair is set whole or refused whole. ONE undo step; a run of calls on the same pair inside the coalescing window (a drag) stays one step. 'x' and 'y' answer each macro's value, applied/skipped counts and writes.

Bind an existing parameter to a macro: 'chain' and 'effect' address a device in the rack's chains (fx-<n> order), 'parameter' is its display name as plugin.param_get reports it, and 'low'/'high' are the window as a fraction (0..1) of the parameter's own range, 'curve' (-1..1, 0 linear) the response across it. Refused when the parameter does not resolve, so a macro never carries a target that can only fail. Reversible through the ProjectJournal.
Unbind one parameter from a macro, by its target index as rack.get_state reports it. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (the recorded undo step re-inserts the captured target at its index).

Drop a parallel chain from a channel's rack. Chain 0 is the channel's own effect chain and is refused. The removed chain's effects and their state are captured in the transaction's before-state. Removing the rack's LAST chain is one undo step that re-creates it with its devices; an inner chain's removal has no automatic undo (the transaction says reversible: false).

Choose the chain a channel's rack routes to: a chain index, or -1 for parallel (every chain runs and the outputs sum). Reversible through the ProjectJournal (an action checkpoint restores the previous selection).

Feed each chain of a channel's parallel rack a part of the signal: 'mode' bands (chain k gets band k, low to high, of a split at 'crossovers' - up to five frequencies in Hz, spread in octaves when fewer are given), mid_side (chain 0 the mid, chain 1 the side), left_right (chain 0 the left, chain 1 the right) or none (every chain the whole signal). The rack's sum puts the parts back together (the bands are Linkwitz-Riley crossovers that sum flat), so empty chains sound as the channel did. Applies while the rack routes in parallel. With no 'mode' it reports the split. Saved with the rack; one undo step.

Wrap devices of a channel's own chain into a new chain of its rack, in order and with their settings: 'plugins' (fx-<n> ids) or, left out, every device. Wrapping every device selects the new chain, so the channel sounds as before and more chains can be layered beside it (rack.add_chain, rack.set_selected parallel); wrapping some makes them a parallel layer beside the devices that stay. A device that cannot be re-created stops the rest: the reply then carries 'stopped' (why) and 'not_wrapped' (how many). One undo step.

Add a key/velocity zone to a channel's rack: an inclusive key range (0..127) and an inclusive velocity range (0..200) mapped to one of the rack's chains, with an optional sample reference. A note of an instrument track playing into the channel that falls into the zone (the first matching zone wins) plays on that chain only; with a sample that loads, the note plays the sample there instead of the instrument ('sample_loaded' in zone_state says whether it loaded - a missing file is kept, not refused). Returns its zone-<n> id. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (an action checkpoint removes the zone this command created).
Drop a zone from a channel's rack. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (the recorded undo step re-inserts the captured zone at its index).

Ask which of a channel's rack zones a note falls into: the first zone, in the order it was added, whose key range and velocity range both contain (key, velocity) - the zone, and so the chain, such a note plays on. Read-only.

Bounce the selection to a new track: the range's tracks (range.set), over its ticks, rendered together into one file ('out', or beside the project) that lands on a new audio track at the range's start; 'mute_sources' (true when left out) mutes the bounced tracks so the song sounds as before. One undo step. This command keeps its synchronous result contract for compatibility; use render.queue_bounce with operation range_bounce for a cancellable job.
Clear the range.

Render each covered sample track's clips inside the range into ONE clip (clip.consolidate per track - clips crossing an edge are refused: range.split first). The tracks' consolidations are one undo step, which control.undo reverts for every track together.
Copy the clips that lie inside the range (range.split first to include the parts of clips crossing its edges). Changes nothing.
Keep only what is inside the range on its tracks. One undo step (every covered track is checkpointed).

Remove what is inside the range on its tracks (clips crossing an edge are split there first); with 'ripple', later clips move left to close the gap. One undo step (every covered track is checkpointed).
Copy what is inside the range and paste it right after it; the range moves onto the copy, so repeating it repeats the pattern. One undo step (every covered track is checkpointed).

Fade the sample clips the range touches: a clip whose start is inside the range fades in over the part of the range it covers, one whose end is inside fades out - across a cut between two clips that is a crossfade. With 'fade_in' / 'fade_out' (ticks) every clip in the range gets those lengths instead (batch fades); 'shape' sets both shapes. One undo step (every covered track is checkpointed).
The range: active, start, end, its tracks, and how many clips are copied.
Insert empty time at the range's start on its tracks - 'length' ticks, default the range's length - moving everything from there later. One undo step (every covered track is checkpointed).
Paste the copied clips at 'position' (default the range's start) onto the range's tracks, in the order they were copied from. One undo step (every covered track is checkpointed).
Select a time range from 'start' to 'end' (ticks) over 'tracks' (trk ids), or over every track ('all', the default with no tracks). Interface state, drawn in the arranger.
Split every clip on the range's tracks at its start and its end. One undo step (every covered track is checkpointed).

Arm one record route: start writing the interleaved input channel it selects into a 24-bit WAV, and journal the take beside it (the take journal is what makes a crashed capture recoverable - record.journal_begin's side file, written here by the recorder's own arm()). 'route' is the route index record.get_state reports; 'input_channel' defaults to the route's own index and must be inside [0, input_channel_capacity) - the FRAMES the route records come from the engine's input path, so with no capture device open and no frames staged the take is silent however the route is armed (record.input_get_state says which of those is true). 'file' must be absolute and defaults to zene-take-route<N>.wav beside this instance's recovery file; 'sample_rate', when given, must be the engine's rate (a take records at the rate the engine runs). Not reversible: control.undo refuses this arm because the take file is outside the project journal. Call record.disarm_track to stop writing; the take remains at the returned file path and can be kept or deleted manually.

Stop every armed record route in one call and report the whole recorder afterwards. Each route's take is flushed and closed and its journal retired, exactly as record.disarm_track does for one. Not reversible: every route's take is a file that stays on disk, and re-arming starts a new one.

Stop one record route: the disk-writer is drained and joined, the WAV is closed, and the take journal is RETIRED - a clean stop leaves no journal, which is what makes 'there is a journal' and 'the capture died' the same fact (include/RecordingJournal.h). The take file stays on disk. This is record.arm_track's explicit stop operation, not its undo inverse, since the WAV remains after a clean stop. Not reversible itself: re-arming writes a NEW take rather than restoring this one, and there is nothing the engine could hand back.

Every record route the engine prepared, and the input path that feeds them. A route is one capture stream: an arm flag, the interleaved input channel it reads, the take file it writes, the take JOURNAL beside it, and the frame counters (pushed / recorded / journalled / overflow / write errors). The engine prepares 64 routes, and each may select ANY of the configured input channels - that pair of numbers (route_count and input_channel_capacity) is the 'arbitrary input count / multiple simultaneous inputs' feature row 64 asks for. `input` is record.input_get_state's own report, including `input_frames_staged` and `wide_frames`: both are 0 under a backend with no capture path, which is what 'a record route takes no inputs' measured. `latency_frames` is the recording round trip - the device's output and input latency plus one capture block of staging - that a take recorded against playback is shifted back by. Read-only.

The engine's capture-IN path, asked directly: what the configuration asks for (device, channel COUNT, which pair of captured channels rides the stereo bus), what this backend actually did with it (capture_capable, capture_open, capture_reason, the channels and rate the device granted), and what the two input stages hold now (bus_frames on the stereo bus, wide_frames/wide_channels on the N-channel stage, plus the staged and dropped counters). 'capture_capable: false' means this instance's backend has no capture path at all; 'capture_capable: true, capture_open: false' means it has one and the device refused - capture_reason carries the device's own message. Read-only, and the honest place to look before blaming a silent take.

Set the capture input path: 'device' (empty = the playback device), 'channels' (1..128 - the ARBITRARY input count of feature row 64), and 'left'/'right' (which two captured channels the stereo engine bus carries, so an interface's third and fourth input can be what the rest of the engine hears). Fields not given keep their current value. The four keys are written to the config file under `audioinput`, exactly as the settings dialog writes its own, and 'restart_required' is true: the backend opens the device at start and the recorder's routes are built when the engine is, so the next start is when this takes effect - there is no live device swap to pretend about. Reversible: the recorded inverse is this command with the previous plan, and control.undo dispatches it (the settings.set precedent, which records a command inverse for the same kind of config write).

Start a journalled capture: write the take journal (<take>.rec-journal) that makes a recording recoverable if this process dies before the capture stops cleanly. `take` must be absolute (a relative path names a different file in the next process). Write the journal, then arm the recorder against the same path, then keep it current with record.journal_update. Reversible: the recorded inverse is the paired command (record.recovery_discard when no journal existed, record.journal_begin with the previous contents when one did), which control.undo dispatches.

End a journalled capture CLEANLY: remove the take journal so the next start does not offer this take as a crashed recording. This is what the recorder's own disarm() does - a clean stop leaves no journal, which is why 'a journal is there' and 'the capture died' are the same fact. Reversible: the recorded inverse is record.journal_begin with the journal that was removed.

Record how much of the take had reached disk at the last flush ('frames_on_disk'), which is the count the recovery offer reports as guaranteed. It must not move backwards: the journal only ever records that MORE of the take reached disk. The recorder's own disk-writer does this every tenth of a second of audio (recordingjournal::updateIntervalFrames), which is the whole of the lag bound. Reversible (paired command).

Refuse an interrupted capture's offer: remove its take journal so the next start stops offering it. THE TAKE'S WAV IS NEVER DELETED - it stays on disk at the take path the transaction's before-state names, which is the documented fallback because this command has no inverse (control.undo fails, typed, naming that path).

Every capture an abnormal exit left behind in `dir` (default: this instance's working directory): one entry per in-progress take journal whose WAV still exists. Each entry reports frames_journalled (what the journal recorded at its last update), frames_in_file (measured from the take's RIFF header, falling back to the file's real length when a crashed header was never updated) and frames_recoverable (the SMALLER of the two - the guaranteed count). The bound travels with every entry: a crash loses at most journal_lag_bound_frames plus one 4096-frame writer batch (0.185 s at 48 kHz, Q050-045) while the disk-writer is healthy; only a STALLED writer can lose up to 65536 frames still in the recorder's ring. Writes nothing.

Bring an interrupted capture into the project: a new sample track named 'Recovered: <take>' holding the recovered file in a clip at bar 1, and the take's journal marked restored so the next start stops offering it. One undo step: control.undo removes the track and puts the offer back, control.redo places it again. The take's WAV is never moved, rewritten or deleted. record.recovery_restore stays the resolve-only verb; File > Recover Recordings and the startup offer run this command.

Take an interrupted capture's offer: report the material the journal recovered and mark the journal `restored`, so the next start stops offering it. The take's WAV is NOT moved, rewritten or deleted - the material stays exactly where the crash left it, and the result says so (`audio_untouched`). This verb only resolves the offer; record.recovery_place is the one that also puts the take on a new sample track, undoably. Reversible: the recorded inverse is record.journal_begin with the journal that was restored.
How long recording can go on: the free space where takes are written, at the rate the armed routes write (24-bit, one channel a route; one route when none is armed), in seconds.

Arm or disarm retrospective AUDIO capture: while armed, the engine keeps the most recent frames of its INPUT BUS in one bounded ring, so the take you did not press record for can still be written with record.retro_capture_to_take. With no 'armed' argument the mode is ARMED; 'armed': false is its disarm. Nothing is recorded while disarmed, and the cost then is one relaxed atomic load per rendered period. The ring is allocated once, when the engine is built ('capacity_frames' in the reply is that allocation, 1048576 frames); a frame that falls out of it is counted in 'overwritten_frames' and cannot be recovered. Mode/engine state, not project state, so no transaction is recorded and control.undo has nothing to reverse (the midi.retro_capture_arm precedent, verb for verb).

What retrospective AUDIO capture is holding: whether it is armed, the ring's capacity in frames and in SECONDS, how many frames are retained right now and how many seconds that is, how many frames have already been overwritten by later audio (the window's bound, as a measurement), frames dropped because a snapshot was in flight, and the count of copies that could not obtain a consistent window. Read-only.

Write the retained window to a 24-bit STEREO WAV - the take that was already played when this command ran. The window is copied under the ring's publication handshake, so the copy is never torn even with the engine running, and the file is written off the audio thread. Refused, typed, when the window holds no frames: a take with no audio in it is not a take. 'file' must be absolute and defaults to zene-retro-take.wav beside this instance's recovery file. NOT reversible and NOT inserted into the session: the file it writes is yours to keep, and turning it into a clip is the project's own load path, not this command's (docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).

Where record route 'route' takes its audio from: 'source' input (the engine's input, its input channel - the default), master (the mix, resampling) or channel (mixer channel 'channel' at 'tap' pre_fx, pre_fader or post_fader); 'side' left or right (a route records one channel). Interface state, not saved with the project. With only 'route' it reports it. One undo step.

Record the engine's configured stereo input straight into an AudioFileProcessor or SlicerT on instrument track 'track'. The take is bounded: it ends when 'seconds' (default 2, at most 30) of input have been taken, or when record.sampler_capture_stop ends it early. The first frames (the recording round trip, 'latency_frames' in the reply) are skipped so the take lines up with what was heard. record.sampler_capture_status follows it; record.sampler_capture_land writes it as a WAV and loads it into the device. 'cancel': true drops the take in hand. Not a project edit: no transaction is recorded.

Land a finished sampler take as a 24-bit stereo WAV. Optional 'file' must be an absolute path that does not exist; without it, a new take is saved in the user's Recordings folder. Load it into the device it was recorded for through the instrument's own loader - AudioFileProcessor shows and plays it, SlicerT recalculates its slices. Refused until record.sampler_capture_status says done. One undo step: it restores the device's previous sample and settings; the WAV stays on disk.

Read the sampler take back: 'state' (idle, recording, done - ready for record.sampler_capture_land), the target track and device, the frames taken and the length it was bounded to, their lengths in seconds, the frames a starved writer dropped, the sample rate and the round trip it was shifted by. Read-only.

End the sampler take in hand early: the input frames taken so far are the take, and record.sampler_capture_land can install it. Idempotent once the take is done. Not a project edit: no transaction is recorded.
Close the reference project.

Copy clips of the reference's track 'track' (index) - 'clips' (indices; every one when left out) - onto this project's track 'to' (trk-<n>): note clips onto an instrument track, audio clips onto a sample track. They keep their positions, or with 'position' (ticks) the first lands there and the rest keep their spacing. One undo step.

Copy devices - 'devices' (indices; every one when left out) of the reference's track 'track' or mixer channel 'channel' (indices; exactly one of the two, naming the source) - onto the end of the chain of 'to' (trk-<n> or ch-<n>) in this project, with their settings. The chain is rebuilt from its document (chain.apply's path), so its device ids renumber. One undo step.

Copy the reference's 'tracks' (indices; every one when left out) into this project - device, effects, clips and automation - as project.import_tracks does: each keeps its mixer channel (by name, a new one made when this project has none) and gets ids of its own. One undo step removes them.

The reference project: its file (and 'stale' when the file changed since it was parsed), its tracks - index, name, type, instrument, clips (index, kind, name, position, length) and devices (index, plugin) - and its mixer channels with their devices.

Open another project file ('path', .mmp / .mmpz) as the reference, beside the session: parsed, browsable, copied from - several projects at once without a second engine. Answers what reference.get_state does. The reference is read-only interface state: never played, never saved with a project, and it stays open across project.open and project.switch.

Bind a MIDI controller's eight knobs to remote-control pages: 'input' (a readable port, as midi.clients_list names it), 'output' (optional - the knobs' values are sent back on a page or device change, for motorised or LED-ring knobs), 'channel' (0-15; any when left out) and 'first_cc' (the first of eight consecutive CCs, default 16). Replaces a connected one; follows the selection until remote.target says otherwise. 'subscribed' says whether the input is a port the MIDI client has (false: nothing will arrive).
Release the remote-control knobs.
Show another page of the device's parameters on the knobs: 'page' (0 = parameters 1-8) or 'delta' (+1 next, -1 previous; +1 when neither is given). Clamped to the pages there are.
What the remote-control knobs drive now: the device, the page and its eight parameters with their values, the page count, the ports and whether they follow the selection.
The device the knobs drive: 'target' (trk-<n> / ch-<n>) and 'plugin' (fx-<n>, or inst - the default - for a track's instrument); 'follow' true makes them follow the selected track or channel.

Batch conversion: queue every audio file of 'files' (absolute) to be written into 'out_dir' as 'format' (wav or flac), at 'sample_rate' (left out: the file's own) and 'bit_depth' (16, 24 - the default - or 32 float, wav only). Runs in the render queue, off the control thread, each with its report.

Queue a render to 'out' (absolute) as 'format': of the session as it is NOW (a snapshot is taken, so later edits do not change it), another project file ('project'), or one track as an output-only bounce ('operation':'bounce' with 'track'). Project renders may cover one range ('start_ticks' and 'end_ticks' together) with the export settings in force. Jobs run one after another in a child process without holding this surface ('start' false queues it without starting the queue now - it runs when the queue next runs); render.queue_list follows them and each ends with a report (bytes, sha256, time, loudness).

Render a track or the selected range in the background, then apply one freeze, land, or flatten edit on the UI thread. Returns a job id immediately; follow it with render.queue_list or render.queue_report and cancel with render.queue_cancel. The task indicator also reports the running phase and Cancel. The target is checked before the output is installed; if it changed, the job fails without changing the project or output. Existing bounce.in_place, freeze.track, freeze.region, bounce.land, track.flatten and range.bounce commands keep their synchronous result contracts for compatibility.
Cancel render-queue job 'job' (or every open job with 'all'): a queued one is dropped, a running render is stopped.
Remove the jobs that have ended from the render queue.
The render queue: every job (render, convert or bounce), its state and phase, bounce progress when known, target ids, file and, once done, its report.
One render-queue job's current state, phase, progress and target ids, or its terminal report: bytes, sha256, seconds taken and the loudness meter's reading of the file (meter.measure_file's payload).

Render the current session to a file and return its hash (headless). Whole project by default; pass start_ticks and end_ticks TOGETHER to render only that span of the song (a selection), in which case the span is rendered exactly - no tail bar and no loop repetition - and the reply reports the range and the frame count. The render is started with the export settings in force: the preset applied through export.preset_apply (sample rate, bit depth, stereo mode), or the render path's own defaults when none is applied. `channels`: 'stereo' (the default; a surround master is folded with the ITU-R BS.775 downmix) or 'surround' - one WAV channel per speaker of the surround master (6 for 5.1, 8 for 7.1, WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE with its channel mask), refused on a stereo master, for a format other than wav, and with the loudness report on; the reply's `channels` and `channel_layout` say what the file holds. Runs in a CHILD process, so the declared bound applies: this surface does not answer - not even control.ping - until it finishes (docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).

Export the song's named sections (section.add/set/list) as separate files: one file per section, named after the section, each rendered to exactly the section's own start..end ticks (no tail bar). The file name is the section's name with the characters a filesystem refuses (/ \ : * ? " < > |) removed and leading dots dropped; trailing dots and spaces become one '_', and a Windows-reserved base name (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9, even with an extension) gets '_' appended to the base (CON -> CON_), the same on every platform. Names that are equal after Unicode canonical decomposition and case folding (Intro/intro) would be one file on Windows and macOS, so the later section gets '-2', then '-3' (intro-2.wav), skipping any name already taken; a name empty once cleaned is its id (sec-<n>). 'out' is an absolute directory the files are written into; 'sections' picks specific sec-<n> ids (default: every section, in time order); 'format' is one of the build's renderable formats (default wav). Each file is rendered through render.render, so the export settings in force - the preset applied through export.preset_apply - set its rate and bit depth; the reply names them and one entry per written file. NOTE the declared bound: each render runs in a child process and this surface does not answer until it finishes (docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).

Export every unmuted track to its own file in an absolute directory: one stem per track, post-fader and post-effects, including that track's own sends and their tails, each rendered to the project's length plus 'tail_bars' bars (default 1, the whole-project render's own convention). The stems are written with the export settings in force - the sample rate, bit depth and stereo mode of the preset applied through export.preset_apply, or the render path's own defaults (44100 Hz, 16-bit, joint stereo) when none is applied; the reply names them. Returns the new file names. NOTE the declared bound: the render runs in a child process and this surface does not answer - not even control.ping - until it finishes (docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).

Compare two revisions of a project, or one revision against the file as it is on disk now (the id 'live', which only this command accepts - revisions.list does not report the working file as a revision). The result reports each side's id, source, timestamp, size and sha256, whether the two are byte-identical, and a STRUCTURAL comparison of the two documents: how many elements of each tag each side holds, the element totals and the tags that differ. That is a summary, not a semantic diff - the musical diff of two project documents is tools/mmpz-git's (`mmpz-git diff`), outside this process. Read-only.

The project's revision timeline: every revision this machine still holds, newest first, each with the SOURCE it came from ('rotation' - the keep-3 revision set project.save rotates, '<file>.rev0..rev2'; 'backup' - the '<file>.bak' a save from the interface writes; 'autosave' - the periodic recover.mmp and the recover.mmp.bak it replaced; 'git' - the commits that touched the file where the project lives in a git repository), its timestamp (UTC; an autosave reports its sidecar's recorded savedUTC), its size and its sha256. Read-only: nothing is written and no new store is created. The `id` each entry carries is what revisions.compare and revisions.restore take. The `git` half is bounded and optional: 'include_git' false, no git on the machine, or no repository, and the `git` object says which - without failing the list.

Restore one revision of the project OVER the file on disk, by the `id` revisions.list reports (rev0..rev2, 'backup', 'autosave', 'autosave_prev' or 'git:<sha>'). The live file is rotated into the keep-3 revision set BEFORE it is replaced, so the restore is itself recoverable - control.undo puts the replaced file back, or, when there was no file on disk yet, removes the one this call created. Refused, typed and without writing anything, when the id names no revision, when the source exceeds the policy's 8 MiB per-revision cap, or when the live file does (its rotation would have to be bounded by the same cap, and a truncated project is a corrupt revision). The session in memory is NOT reloaded: call project.open afterwards to work on the restored bytes.
The piano-roll view of a clip: the clip and every note with its position, length, key and velocity. Without 'clip', the selected clip is used.

The routing graph a target's signal is processed through: the nodes and their type names, the connections, the cached topological order the audio thread walks, the output node, and - for a mixer channel - its rack's graph. Read-only.
The routing matrix: every channel (id, name, position) with its sends - to, amount, pre-fader, on or off. Read only.
What uses a channel: the tracks playing into it, the channels sending into it and the channels it sends to. Read only.

Accept the offer of a normal start: write the acknowledgement the NEXT launch consumes, so it loads with third-party plugins enabled. Keeps the marker and does not change this session (instances already skipped were never created). Refuses unless this session started safe - the offer is made in a safe session and nowhere else. Not reversible - no function in this engine removes the acknowledgement except safestart.clear, which removes the marker with it.

Clear the crash marker: delete the marker and the acknowledgement, so the next launch is a normal one, and leave safe-start mode in this session. The verb for 'the cause is known and fixed'. Refuses when there is neither file, so a call that would change nothing writes nothing. Not reversible - the marker's own record of the crashed session is gone; control.undo names the fallback.

Safe-start mode's state: whether the module is installed, the crash marker and the acknowledgement as files (path, existence, size, time), whether a marker says the previous run did not exit cleanly, whether THIS session started safe, how many sessions in a row have, the session-scoped skip switch, every plugin instance the mode skipped and why, the directories the third-party classification treats as this build's own, the previous session's own record and the offer of a normal start. Read-only, and it answers in every configuration.

Turn the load-time skip of third-party plugin INSTANCES on or off for THIS session - the session-scoped half of the predicate Plugin::instantiate consults. Does not touch the marker: with it off, a project loaded now loads its third-party plugins when it is opened (already-skipped instances are not created by this call). Re-armed by the next session. Not reversible - process-scoped mode state, no journal checkpoint, and nothing puts an already-skipped instance back.

Bake a gain change into a sample clip's source: every frame multiplied by the requested dB, swapped in through SampleClip::setSampleBuffer as a transformed COPY - the previous buffer is never modified, so a second clip sharing it keeps its audio, and one control.undo re-loads the previous source. No limiter is applied (the float pipeline keeps values past 0 dBFS); sample.normalize is the peak-targeted bake, clip.set_gain the non-baking alternative and sample.edit_range the selected-range gain. A sample clip's Process menu offers it as Amplify..., and agents reach the same command on the control socket and through MCP (docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).

Discard the source frames outside an audio clip's window: a fresh buffer of just what the clip plays replaces its source, so it sounds the same and stores less. Never written into a buffer another clip shares. One undo step (Clip checkpoint).

Edit an audio clip's source over source frames ['from', 'to'): 'op' gain ('gain_db'), silence, delete (the rest closes up), reverse, fade_in, fade_out or crop (keep only the range) - the sample editor's operations - or 'mono', which converts the WHOLE source (from 0, to the frame count) with the documented per-frame arithmetic mean (L + R) / 2 on both playback sides, keeping the rate, frame count and clip settings and reporting channels/layout - 'mono' needs only 'clip' (absent from/to default to the whole source), while every range op requires both bounds. A fresh copy of the source is swapped in, never a buffer another clip shares. One undo step (Clip checkpoint).

Bake a LINEAR fade into a sample clip's source: direction=in ramps 0 -> unity across the whole source, direction=out ramps unity -> 0, both channels together. The result replaces the source through SampleClip::setSampleBuffer as a transformed COPY and one control.undo re-loads the previous source. This whole-source bake has no range parameter, so it always spans the whole clip source and has only the linear curve; the Sample Editor's selected-range fades are sample.edit_range's fade_in / fade_out, and clip.set_fade remains the non-baking window fade. A sample clip's Process menu offers it as Fade, in or out (docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).

Generate a buffer (kind: tone, white noise, pink noise or silence) into a NEW audio clip on a sample track, routed through the non-destructive clip model: Track::createClip makes the clip and SampleClip::setSampleBuffer hands it the source, so an existing clip's audio is never overwritten (decision design/specs/DECISION-706-DESTRUCTION-MODEL.md). One journal checkpoint before the clip exists: one control.undo removes clip and buffer together. length is in ticks, position the clip's start; frequency (Hz) and amplitude (0..1) reach the tone and noise kinds - silence ignores them. In the interface a sample track's More menu - the track header's and the Inspector's - offers it as Insert Test Signal..., which opens this command's form with that track fixed and position 0, length 192 and kind tone as the starting values; confirming creates the clip. Agents reach the same command on the control socket, through MCP and from a script; the Sample Editor's range operations are sample.edit_range (docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).
Give an audio clip its own copy of its source, so a later bake of a duplicate that shares it cannot change this one. One undo step (Clip checkpoint).

Bake a level change that puts the sample clip's peak at target_dbFS (default 0): the peak across both channels is measured, one scale factor is applied to every frame, and the result replaces the source through SampleClip::setSampleBuffer as a transformed COPY. A silent source is REFUSED with the measured peak - there is no scale factor to apply - and one control.undo re-loads the previous source. A sample clip's Process menu offers it as Normalize... (docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).

Bake a reversal into a sample clip's source: the frame order is reversed, both channels together, and the result replaces the source through SampleClip::setSampleBuffer as a transformed COPY - the previous buffer is never modified and one control.undo re-loads it, so the command is its own documented inverse rather than a flag to toggle. A sample clip's Process menu offers it as Reverse (docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).
An audio clip's frequency content: 'rows' (128) moments evenly over the clip, each 'bands' (64) log-spaced bands from 30 Hz to Nyquist, in dB - what a spectrogram view draws. Read only.

Write a sample clip's whole stereo source as two mono WAV files (float32, at the source rate): 'left_path' receives the left channel and 'right_path' the right channel, sample for sample, with no resampling, trimming or mixing. The clip and the project are not changed. Both paths are .wav files and must differ; a mono clip is refused.
The scales defined with scale.define, each with its degrees.

Define a scale of your own: 'name' and 'degrees' (semitone offsets 0..11 from the root; the root is added when missing). scale.set, the scale snap and note.transpose_in_key take it by name. Without 'degrees' it removes the scale. Kept in the config file; one undo step.

The key and scale (major or minor) a clip's notes fit best, weighted by how long each sounds, with the two runners-up and how much of the music each holds ('fit', 0..1). Read only; scale.set takes the answer.

Set the CONTEXT's root and scale from the key detect.apply stored in the project (`<detected-key>`): the detected tonic becomes the root and its scale the scale. Refused NotFound when no key has been detected. Reversible: a recorded action step restores the previous root and scale.

What this group is resolving against: the context's root, scale name, degrees, pitch classes and mask. Naming 'root' and/or 'scale' answers for those instead and says so ('resolved_from_arguments'), without changing the context. A 'clip' argument adds the analysis an arranging caller wants - how many of its notes are in the scale and how many are out, counted with the engine's own predicate (NoteTransform::matches) - so "this part is in key" is a measurement. A context with no scale set yet reports an empty 'scale', an empty mask and scale_set:false. Read-only.

Every scale this engine knows and the twelve keys, with each scale's degrees (semitone offsets from the root), its pitch classes, its twelve-character membership mask (index 0 = C, so "101011010101" is the major scale: C D E F G A B, ChordTable's own scale row) and its size. The vocabulary is the scales are the ones with more than six degrees; 'include_chords' adds the chord entries too. 'root' (a key index 0..11 or a name such as "C#"/"Db") shifts every pitch class and every mask; absent, the group's own context root answers. Read-only.

Set the CONTEXT's root - the key every later scale.snap_notes and every scale.get_state resolves against when it names no root. Accepts a key index 0..11 or a name ("C", "c", "C#", "Db", "D♭", or the piano roll's "C# / Db" spelling; an octave suffix is ignored, because a root here is a pitch class). An unknown name is refused rather than defaulted to C. Reversible: a recorded action step restores the previous root. The context is this group's own process state and is deliberately not serialized - it is NOT the piano roll's key selector (docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).

Set the CONTEXT's scale by NAME - a scale this engine knows, from scale.list (e.g. "Major", "Minor", "Major pentatonic"). An empty string CLEARS the context's scale, after which scale.snap_notes refuses instead of guessing. A name ChordTable does not carry is refused typed (NotFound), not resolved to an empty scale. Reversible: a recorded action step restores the previous scale. The context is this group's own process state and is deliberately not serialized - it is NOT the piano roll's scale selector (docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).

Move every note of a clip (or of the current selection) whose pitch class is OUTSIDE the scale to the nearest in-scale pitch, clamped to the MIDI range, with a tie resolving downward; notes already in the scale are left alone (NoteTransform::snapToScale, the engine's own rule). The scale is the CONTEXT's unless this call names 'root' and/or 'scale', and a call with no scale anywhere is REFUSED rather than snapped to a guessed key. The report says how many notes moved and how many are still out of scale afterwards, so "it is in key now" is a measurement. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (MidiClip checkpoint) - and NOT by re-running the snap, which is why the checkpoint is the inverse. 'scope' is 'clip' (default) or 'selection'.
The Lua scripts this build ships (data/scripts, resolved through the app's own 'data:' search path) with their sizes and hashes. Reads the filesystem, so it answers before the engine is up.

Run a Lua script (docs/specs/SPEC-lua-api-v0.md) in this running instance - the same ScriptEngine the run-and-exit `--run-script` CLI flag drives, on its own worker thread with the engine apply side pumped on the UI thread. Returns the Lua log lines, or a typed error carrying them. 'budget' overrides the per-invocation instruction budget (default from the engine) for this call only. The project is captured whole before the script runs (bounded by the undo stack's byte budget, control.set_undo_depth; over it the run is REFUSED before anything changes), and everything the script changed is ONE undo step: control.undo restores the exact pre-script project and control.redo reapplies the run's result.

Set the block of memory a script run may hold, in bytes (CODE-6): the budget beside the instruction budget. The Lua state is opened with an allocator that refuses any allocation past this cap, so a runaway script fails with 'memory budget exceeded' and its run is aborted - it cannot grow until the machine kills the process. Refuses a value outside [min_memory_budget, max_memory_budget]; there is no 'unlimited' through this surface. Reversible: one control.undo restores the previous cap (script.run reports the budget and what the last run measured).
Add a section from 'start' to 'end' (ticks) - a verse, a chorus - with a 'name' and an optional 'color'. Drawn as a lane over the arranger, saved with the project. One undo step.
The song's sections in time order: id (sec-<n>), start, end, name, colour.
Remove section 'section'. One undo step.
Select section 'section' as the arranger's range (over 'tracks', or every track), so it can be copied, bounced, looped or deleted as one. Through range.set.
Move, resize, rename or recolour section 'section' (only the fields given change). One undo step.

Select saved selection 'name' again: its range (range.set) and those of its clips that still exist ('missing' counts the rest; 'restored' and 'skipped' name the parts that came back and those that did not).
The project's saved selections, in the order they were saved, their 'count' and limit ('max_entries'), and what one never keeps ('not_kept').
Forget one of the project's saved selections ('name'). One undo step.

Save the selection as 'name': the range and the clips selected in the arranger (or 'clips', a list of clip ids; refused NotFound naming one that is not in the project) - 'captures' lists the parts kept, 'not_kept' what a saved selection never keeps (notes, automation points, mixer channels, the play position) - replacing one of that name ('replaced') unless 'replace' is false, when a name in use is refused; at most 99 ('changed' false when it was already saved just so: no undo step). Refused when nothing is selected. Saved with the project; one undo step.
