Arm (or disarm) Arrangement Record: while it is armed the audio thread pushes one event per session launch and per stop into the engine's ring, at the tick the transition fired on. Disarming KEEPS what the ring already carries - the performance is landed, not dropped - and a reset (session.stop_all, session.back_to_arrangement) records the stop of every slot it ends, so a stopped performance has no launches left open. Mode state, not project state: no transaction is recorded.

Land the recorded performance: pair every recorded launch with the stop that ended it and create ONE arrangement clip per pair on that column's song track, at the recorded ticks. REFUSED - consuming nothing - while any recorded start is still open, because a half-landed performance would lose starts or invent their ends; stop the session first (session.stop_all, or session.back_to_arrangement). Also REFUSED without consuming anything when MIDI or audio content cannot be copied to the destination track or an audio source cannot be loaded. Reversible: one composite ProjectJournal checkpoint covering all touched tracks, so one control.undo takes the whole pass back.

Read Arrangement Record back: whether the tap is armed, how many events it has recorded, how many it dropped because the ring was full, how many are waiting, how many clips a land pass would write, and how many launches are still playing (which is what a land pass refuses on). 'pending' is a bounded estimate - the two ring indices are read separately, so a push landing between them is not counted. Read-only.

The Back-to-Arrangement switch: end the session playback and hand every track back to its arrangement content (SPEC A1 mutual exclusivity - a track plays its session content or its arrangement content, never both). It is one atomic request, the same engine operation session.stop_all makes, and it exists as its own id because it is the ARRANGEMENT's verb: the reply reports the recorded performance, which this does NOT drop - the ring is landed afterwards by session.arrangement_record_land. Not a project edit: no transaction is recorded.

Bind a note ('key' 0..127, 'channel' 0..15 or -1 for any) to a launcher action: 'action' slot (with 'track' and 'scene' - the note's release releases a Gate or Repeat cell), scene (with 'scene') or stop_all. Replaces a binding on the same note. Kept in the config file; one undo step.

Bind a MIDI NOTE or CONTROL CHANGE to a built-in command that needs no arguments, and run it through the registry once per activation. 'trigger' is note (with 'key' 0..127) or cc (with 'controller' 0..127); 'channel' is 0..15 or -1 for any; 'command' is a registered command id whose schema requires no arguments (the control change's value is NOT passed on as one). A note fires on its press and rearms on its release; a control change fires when it leaves zero and rearms at zero, so a sweep is one activation. Replaces a binding on the same control, and a note still bound to the launcher is taken away from it by the same edit (one undo step). Kept in the config file.
Bind the next note the connected controller plays to a launcher action ('action', 'track', 'scene' as session.bind).
The launcher's controller bindings, whether a controller is connected and what the next note will be bound to (session.bind_learn).

Open a MIDI controller for the launcher's bindings: 'input' (a readable port, as midi.clients_list names it), 'output' optional. Its notes then launch what they are bound to. 'subscribed' says whether the input is a port the MIDI client has (false: nothing will arrive).
Make a new scene row from the cells playing now: each playing column's cell is copied into it ('name', Captured when left out). One undo step.

Record what was just played into a launcher cell ('track', 'scene'): the MIDI kept by midi.retro_capture_arm becomes a new pattern - in the clip of pattern-store instrument 'instrument' (0, the first, when left out), 'bars' long (the playing rounded up to whole bars when left out) - and the cell plays that pattern. One undo step.

Empty the whole Session View: no grid, no slot, no scene override, default quantisation. A project that never used the session then re-saves byte-identically (the <session> block is dropped). Reversible through the ProjectJournal.
Empty one grid cell, whatever it held. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (action checkpoint on the <session> block).
The controller's command bindings (what session.bind_command made), and whether a controller is connected.

Read the Follow Action engine back: `follow_actions_enabled` is Live's global toggle (with it off every chain is inert, not cleared), which cells are armed (the count and the bit(track * 8 + scene) mask), how many actions have fired, what the newest fire did (its outcome, the chain entry that produced it, the scene it addressed and the tick it was scheduled for), and - when track and scene are given - that cell's own state and the chain's action time. The mask is a decimal string because a 64-bit mask does not survive a JSON number. Read-only.

Arm (or clear, with enabled: false) one cell's Follow Action chain: the engine stores the chain and evaluates it while the cell plays, firing at the chain's action time. Without 'actions' the cell's own persisted chain is used, which is what session.set_slot wrote. Refused rather than truncated when the chain is longer than the engine's table. 'queued' is the model thread's answer; armed_cells and the rest are the engine's published reading, up to one audio period later. Not a project edit: no transaction is recorded.

The Session View: grid dimensions, the global launch quantisation, every non-empty clip slot with its launch settings, every scene override, and the launch engine's read-back (completed launches, the grid line the newest starts fired on, how many clips started on that one line), `columns`: every column that is launching, playing or stopping and the scene it is on, and `subscenes`: each sub-scene {subscene, name, scene, tracks} (session.subscene_create).
Move a playing cell: it continues from 'position_ticks' into its clip (192 a bar in 4/4), at once. A cell that is not playing is left alone. Not a project edit.
Launch, in 'scene', every cell of the tracks inside the folder track at column 'track' (its sub-folders too) - a group's cells as one. Not a project edit.

Trigger every non-empty clip in one scene row at once and report the tick each was scheduled for. `in_sync` is true when every launched clip resolved to the SAME grid line, which is what a scene launch means; `sync_tick` names that line. Not a project edit: no transaction is recorded.

Trigger one clip slot: queue a launch, quantised to the slot's own (or the supplied) boundary, and report the tick it was scheduled for. The engine records the start when the clock reaches that line. Not a project edit: no transaction is recorded.
The patterns a MIDI launcher cell can play: each pattern's number - session.set_slot's 'pattern' - and the name of its pattern track. Read-only.

Record audio into an empty launcher cell ('track', 'scene') of an audio (sample) track's column: the cell is armed and launched, so the take starts on the launch quantisation's grid line ('quantisation', else the cell's own, else the session's). It takes the engine's stereo input, shifted by the recording round trip, until the cell stops - session.stop_slot's quantised stop, another cell on the column, session.stop_all - or for 'bars' bars. session.record_slot_status follows it; session.record_slot_land makes it the cell's clip. 'cancel': true drops the take in hand (whichever cell it is for) and stops its cell. Not a project edit: no transaction is recorded.

Land a finished launcher-cell take: write it as a 24-bit WAV ('file', absolute; a new take in the user's Recordings folder when left out) and make it the cell's audio clip, named 'name' (the file's name when left out). Refused until session.record_slot_status says done. One undo step: it puts the cell back; the WAV stays on disk.

Read the launcher cell's audio recording back: 'state' (idle, armed - waiting for its launch, recording, finishing - stopped and running on to its length, done - ready for session.record_slot_land), the cell, the grid line it started on, the frames taken and the length it will have, the frames a starved writer dropped, the sample rate and the round trip it was shifted by. Read-only.
Let go of a cell: the release half of a press, which stops a Gate cell and ends a Repeat cell's retriggering (Trigger and Toggle cells ignore it). Not a project edit.

Arm (or clear, with enabled: false) one SCENE's Follow Action chain. While that scene is the launched row (session.launch_scene), its chain fires at the action time and moves every column playing the row together - Stop, PlayAgain, or the row-addressing actions - and it takes precedence over the chains of the row's cells. Linked timing is the row's longest cell loop, one bar when none has one. Without 'actions' the scene's own persisted chain (session.set_scene follow_actions) is used. Not a project edit: no transaction is recorded.

Turn Follow Actions on or off for the WHOLE session: with 'enabled' false every cell's chain is inert - nothing fires - while the chains stay installed, so turning it back on resumes them where they were rather than restarting them. Engine state, not project state: not saved with the project and not journalled, so there is no undo step to reverse. session.follow_get_state reports it back.

Resize the Session View grid (column = a song track, row = a scene). Existing cells keep their content and position; new cells are empty. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (action checkpoint on the <session> block).

Play 'scenes' one after another: each one's chain jumps to the next after 'bars' (the row's length when left out); the last stops, or with 'loop' goes back to the first. 'clear' takes the chains off those scenes instead. The chains are the scenes' own (session.set_scene follow_actions), armed at once. One undo step.
Set the session's global launch quantisation - the grid line every slot whose own quantisation is 'global' waits for. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (action checkpoint on the <session> block).

Set one scene's name and/or its tempo and time-signature overrides; a field that is supplied is written and its override switched on, a field that is not is left alone; `tempo_override` / `timesig_override` switch an override on or off (false keeps the stored value, inactive); `color` ("#rrggbb", empty clears it) colours the scene. `follow_actions` replaces the scene's own Follow Action chain ([] clears it); session.scene_follow_set arms it. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (action checkpoint).

Define one grid cell: a MIDI clip ('type':'midi' + 'pattern'), an audio clip ('type':'audio' + 'source'), or empty ('type':'empty'); plus its launch mode, launch quantisation and playback settings, and `follow_actions`, the cell's persisted Follow Action chain ([] clears it; session.follow_set arms it). Only the fields supplied are written. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (action checkpoint on the <session> block).
The setlist: an ordered list of project files to play through ('items' replaces it), and the entry open now. A preference, kept in the config file, not in any project; a change is one undo step.
Open the setlist's 'to' entry: next (the default), previous, or an index. The project is opened as project.open opens it.

Drop every launched slot on the audio thread's next period, whichever scene or clip it came from. It is one atomic request, so it is safe while the transport runs. Not a project edit: no transaction is recorded.
Stop one clip slot at its next quantisation boundary. A slot that never started stays idle, so this is safe to call unguarded. Not a project edit: no transaction is recorded.

Make a sub-scene: a named subset of one scene's cells - the cells of 'scene' in the columns 'tracks' - that launches on its own (session.subscene_launch). 'name' defaults to "Sub-scene N". Its number is its place in session.get_state's 'subscenes'. One undo step.
Delete sub-scene 'subscene' (the later ones move up one place); its cells are untouched. One undo step.

Launch sub-scene 'subscene': each of its cells exactly as session.launch_scene launches it - with the scene's quantisation (the cell's own, Global meaning the session's), or 'quantisation' / 'mode' for all of them - so they land on the lines the whole scene would. The other columns play on, and the row is not marked as the launched scene (its scene chain does not fire). 'skipped' names the columns with nothing to launch. Not a project edit.
Rename sub-scene 'subscene' to 'name'. One undo step.
Remove the binding on a note ('key', 'channel' - -1 for an any-channel binding). One undo step.
Remove the command binding on a note ('trigger' note, 'key', 'channel') or a control change ('trigger' cc, 'controller', 'channel'). One undo step.
Back the settings up to 'file' (JSON): the preferences, the appearance and the interface's customisations - never folder paths or device names. Writes the file only.

Read one UI/engine setting by the key the config file uses, '<class>/<attribute>' (for example audioengine/audiodev, ui/saveinterval, app/configured). 'value' is the config file's own string form and 'present' says whether the key is set at all rather than defaulted.
Put a backup from 'file' (settings.export's format) back; keys that are not known settings are ignored and listed. One undo step.
Switch to settings preset 'name'. Settings read at start take effect at the next start. One undo step.
The settings presets: each one's name and how many settings it holds.
Forget settings preset 'name'. One undo step.
Keep the current settings as preset 'name' (replacing one of that name; at most 32), in the config file. One undo step.
Find settings by any words of their name, page or key ('text'; every setting when empty): key, page, title, value and whether it is set. The keys are settings.get / settings.set's.

Write one UI/engine setting by its config-file key and persist the config file, exactly as the settings dialog does on OK. 'value' is the config file's own string form (booleans are "1"/"0"). Settings the engine reads at startup (audioengine/audiodev, samplerate, ...) take effect on the next start. The write is recorded with the previous value as its inverse, but ConfigManager is not journalled, so control.undo cannot reverse it.
Write the shortcut set - the menu overrides, the panel overrides and every binding - to 'file' as JSON, for another machine or a backup. Writes only that file.

Apply a shortcut set: the overrides in 'file' (written by shortcuts.export) or given as 'overrides', plus a stage-1 'panels' object; merged over the current ones, or replacing them with 'replace'. Ids this build's actions do not have are kept and listed in 'unknown'; a value that is no key sequence is left out and listed in 'invalid'; 'conflicts' lists the keys more than one action of one scope holds afterwards ({keys, ids, scope}). One undo step.

Every action that can carry a keyboard shortcut: the menu actions ('scope' empty) and the arranger's, note editor's, automation editor's and Perform's own actions ('scope' names which - the same key may differ in each). A binding is its id, its scope, the registry command it declares, its current keys, the code's own default and whether the user overrode it; 'conflict' names the actions of the SAME scope already on those keys (a clash to resolve, while the same key in another scope is not one). 'query' filters by id, keys, command or scope; 'scope' keeps one context. 'conflict_count' is how many rows clash.

Apply a shipped keyboard map ('preset': accessibility, ableton-live, fl-studio or logic-pro) to the matching Zene menu actions. Before the map is replaced, the current set is written to a timestamped shortcuts-backup JSON file in the workspace and its path is reported; shortcuts.import can restore it. One undo step also restores the previous overrides. The backup file remains after that undo, deliberately.

The shipped keyboard maps: the accessibility one and the Ableton Live, FL Studio and Logic Pro migration maps, each by id, name, description and mapping count. They map Zene's corresponding menu actions only, never another DAW's project or settings.

Give one action ('id') - or, without it, every action of one context ('scope': that panel's bindings; the menu map when 'scope' is empty) - its own default shortcut back; with no 'id' and no 'scope' argument at all, every menu AND panel binding. One undo step.

Bind an action to 'keys' (portable text such as "Ctrl+Shift+K"; empty unbinds it) - a menu action, or one of a panel scope's actions ('scope' arranger, note_editor, automation_editor or perform). Refused, typed, when another action of the SAME scope already has those keys - unless 'force', which moves them here and unbinds the other; a binding in another scope is never touched. Kept in the config file (ui/shortcuts), applied at once, one undo step.

The offline stem-separation engine's own facts: the inference backend this build drives (`onnxruntime-cpp` when the ONNX Runtime SDK was found at configure time, otherwise `external-process (python onnxruntime)`), whether it can run right now (`available`, with the reason in `error` when it cannot - the model file is usually what is missing, and models are never bundled), whether a job would fetch the pinned model itself on first use (`fetch_on_first_use`: the model is absent, the default spec is pinned, LMMS_STEM_MODEL does not name a file and LMMS_STEM_OFFLINE is unset - owner decision 14), the model path the store resolves, the model contract's constants (44100 Hz, the 343980-frame / 7.8 s segment) and `realtime: false` with the reason: HTDemucs needs the whole segment as context, so separation is an OFFLINE job and there is no live mode. NOTE: the whole `stem.*` group is compiled only when WANT_STEM_SPLIT is ON - the default since owner decision 14; a build configured with it OFF has no such ids at all (docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).

Ask the worker to stop an outstanding separation job and report its state after the request. Cancellation is cooperative and observed between inference segments, so a running job answers `cancel_requested` first and settles as `cancelled` (poll `stem.job_status`); a job still queued is cancelled immediately. A job that already finished is refused, naming its state, rather than reported as cancelled.

Write the four stems of a COMPLETED job into an absolute directory as `<stem>.wav` (drums, bass, other, vocals - the model contract's fixed order), float32 RIFF/WAVE, and report each file's name, frames, seconds, bytes and sha256. Refuses a job that is not completed, naming its state (a failed job's message is in `stem.job_status`), and refuses an id this instance never issued. A directory that does not exist is created; a file of the same name is overwritten and its reported hash is the one on disk after the write. This writes OUTPUT ARTEFACTS and no project state - building tracks from the files is a separate, deliberate step.

Queue one offline 4-stem separation of an absolute audio FILE (drums, bass, other, vocals) and return its job id immediately - the engine runs on its own worker thread, so the control surface keeps answering while the job runs. The source must be stereo; a rate other than the model's own 44100 Hz is resampled to it first (offline, the engine's best sinc converter), so the stems come back at 44100 Hz. Refused, typed, when the file is missing or undecodable, or when the engine cannot run at all (no python onnxruntime, or the model absent and not fetchable). An absent model that IS fetchable (see `stem.get_state` `fetch_on_first_use`) does not refuse: the job fetches the pinned 166 MB file on its own worker first (`fetching_model`, `download_progress`), then separates. `quality` picks how much consecutive model segments overlap: `fast` 25% (about 2/3 of the inference passes), `standard` 50% (the default, and the only behaviour before the setting existed) or `high` 75% (about twice the passes, each frame averaged over more predictions); the job reports the effective `quality`, `overlap` and `hop_frames`, and `inference_quality` (the setting its worker handed the backend; empty until inference starts). NOT realtime, by nature: HTDemucs needs a 7.8 s lookahead. Follow with `stem.job_status`, then `stem.job_result`.

One separator job by `job_id`, or every job this instance has run when `job_id` is omitted: each job's `state` (queued, running, cancel_requested, completed, cancelled, failed), `progress` (0..1), `fetching_model` and `download_progress` (0..1) while a first job fetches the model, its source, frame count, the effective `quality` / `overlap` / `hop_frames` it runs at, `inference_quality` (what the worker handed the backend) and `since_submit_seconds` (the surface's own wall clock, not a claim about inference time), and `error` when it failed. Reads the manager's atomics, so it answers even while a job is running - this is the poll that proves the control surface is not held by the work.

Fetch a model file into the store (default directory, or `dest_dir`), HTTPS only, verifying the pinned SHA-256 and size BEFORE the file is moved into place - a partial or mismatched download never replaces a good file. With no arguments it fetches the store's own pinned default spec; with any of `url`, `sha256` or `size_bytes` it fetches a caller spec, which must be pinned in full. A file already in place that verifies against the pinned spec is not fetched again (`fetched: false`), offline or not; any other call is refused in offline mode (LMMS_STEM_OFFLINE). A stem job does not need this verb: it fetches the default model itself on first use, on the job's worker thread. DECLARED BOUND: a performing call is a real network transfer on the control surface's own thread, so the surface does not answer - `control.ping` included - until it finishes or fails (the same defect the child-process renders carry, docs/RENDER-CHILD-WAIT.md); the transfer is not exercised by any registered proof, which runs offline so CI never fetches 166 MB.

The model store's own facts: the directory and path it resolves (honouring LMMS_STEM_MODEL and LMMS_STEM_MODEL_DIR), whether the file is present and its size, the spec it would download (`name`, `url`, `sha256`, `size_bytes`, `license`, `license_url`, `model_card_url`, `pinned`) and whether that spec could be downloaded at all (`download_allowed` + `download_reason`). The default spec is PINNED (HTDemucs fp16, MIT, one commit of the model card's repository, SHA-256 and size) and a stem job fetches it on first use, off the control thread; LMMS_STEM_OFFLINE turns that off and reports `download_allowed: false`. Models are never bundled with the product. With `hash: true` the file's SHA-256 is computed and reported (`matches_spec` is null when there is nothing pinned to compare against) - it is off by default because hashing a 166 MB model must be a decision, not a side effect of a read.

Materialise the four stems of a COMPLETED job (drums, bass, other, vocals - the model contract's fixed order) as four SampleTracks, each carrying a clip of its stem at `position` (ticks, default 0) and named `name - <stem>`. This is the user-facing 'Split to stems' result and the SAME command the GUI action calls; the four tracks are ONE undo step, so one `control.undo` removes them all. This edits the project, unlike `stem.job_result`, which writes output WAVs and touches no project state. Refuses a job that is not completed, naming its state, and refuses an id this instance never issued. The stems are the job's shared, immutable buffers, so the redo rebuilds the tracks without copying audio.
Show the tracks from 'bank' on the surface's strips (the bank and channel buttons do the same).

Connect a Mackie Control Universal surface: 'input' and 'output' name the MIDI client's ports (surface.mcu_ports). Its eight strips are a bank of the song's instrument and sample tracks from 'bank': faders set volume, V-pots pan, mute / solo / rec / select and the transport buttons run the registry's own commands, and the motor faders and LEDs follow. The strip LCD (SysEx) is not sent. Replaces a connected surface. Device state: not recorded.
Disconnect the control surface.
The MIDI client's input and output ports, by the names surface.mcu_connect takes.
The control surface: connected or not, its ports, its bank, the track each strip drives and how many events came in and went out.

Stop task 'id' (task.list), if its job can be stopped: a queued one is dropped, a running one stops at its next safe point and removes what it had written. Refused for a task that has ended or whose job runs to its end (a mastering run). The project is not touched.
Forget every ended task in the list (done, failed or cancelled); running and queued ones stay. Session state.

The long jobs of this session, oldest first - render-queue renders and conversions, stem splits, mastering runs, library indexing, video audio extraction - each {id, kind, title, status, progress (0..1, or -1 while the job cannot say), state (queued, running, done, failed, cancelled), cancellable, started_ms, finished_ms}, and how many are 'active'. What the status bar's Tasks list shows. Read-only.

Show the list of background jobs - the status bar's Tasks list ('shown' false hides it; it toggles when left out): each job's title, state, progress and Cancel where the job supports it. It never blocks the window: Escape or a click elsewhere closes it. Interface state.

Open the telemetry consent screen - the Help menu's "Telemetry - what we send..." action, with the live preview of the exact payload. A13/UnattendedRun: this one is a modal screen, so it declares `requires: display, human` and every unattended caller is refused, typed, before the handler runs - an agent can never consent on the user's behalf. Read the state with telemetry.status.

Read-only: whether telemetry is compiled in, whether consent is on, which groups are on, and the exact payload submit() would send (the same bytes the consent screen previews). This is the agent's way to see the telemetry state without being able to change it - consent stays a human act.
Write the theme - every colour role as it will be drawn - to 'file' (JSON), to keep or share. Writes the file only.

The interface's colours as the next start will draw them: the palette, the user's overrides, every colour role {name, color, overridden}, the declared text/surface pairs that fall below their WCAG contrast, when the colours take effect ('applies' next_start, 'restart_required', 'applies_note') and whether the running interface still draws other colours ('restart_pending').

Take a theme's colours from 'file' (theme.export's format) - or from 'colors', {role: #rrggbb} - on top of the current overrides, or instead of them with 'replace'. Every name must be a colour role. Applies from the next start; one undo step. A change that would put a text/surface pair below WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text and controls) that met it before is refused, naming the pairs - unless 'allow_low_contrast' is true; the reply lists them either way ('new_contrast_failures').
Drop every colour override: the chosen palette as shipped, from the next start. One undo step.

Give colour role 'name' (theme.get lists them: panel, text, accent, ...) the colour 'color' (#rrggbb), or with 'color' empty put the palette's own back. Applies from the next start; a preference in the config file, one undo step. A change that would put a text/surface pair below WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text and controls) that met it before is refused, naming the pairs - unless 'allow_low_contrast' is true; the reply lists them either way ('new_contrast_failures').
Append a track of the given type (default instrument) and return its stable trk-<n> id. Undo removes the track; redo recreates it with a fresh stable trk-<n> id.
An instrument track's articulations, in order (a note's 'articulation' is the 1-based index into this list).

Set an instrument track's articulations (its expression map): a list of {name, keyswitch?, program?, controller?, value?} - what is sent, just before a note that asks for the articulation (note.edit 'articulation', 1-based), to switch the instrument: a keyswitch key, a program change, a control change. An empty list clears the map. A note asks for an articulation by its position, so 'from' (optional) gives, per new entry, its position in the old map (0 for a new one): the notes then follow their articulation when entries are moved, and ask for none when theirs is removed (without it they keep their numbers). The reply's 'notes_remapped' counts the notes changed. One undo step - the notes included.

Build a drum rack: 'pads' [{sample (a file), key (0..127; 36 upward when left out), name}] - each pad a sampler track playing its sample at its key, inside one folder named 'name', and each playing into a mixer channel of its own (the pad's chain, for its inserts) that sends to one bus channel, the rack's output. Answers the folder, the pad tracks, the bus and the channels. One undo step.

Read a drum rack back: 'track' is its folder. Answers the folder, its name, the bus its pads send to and 'pads', each {track, name, sample (absolute path; empty when embedded), key (the trigger key: the note that plays the sample at its own pitch), channel (the pad's own chain), sends_to, playback {amp, start, end, loop_start, loop, reversed, stutter, interpolation, attack (ms), release (ms), voice_limit}} - what the project saves. Writes nothing.

Add a sample pad to a drum rack: 'track' is the rack's folder, 'sample' a file, 'name' (the file's name when left out), 'key' (0..127; the next after 36 when left out). The pad is a sampler track in the folder with a channel of its own sending to the rack's bus. Answers the pad's state as track.drum_rack_get_state reads it. One undo step.
Edit a drum-rack pad: 'track' is the pad, and any of 'name', 'key' (the trigger key, 0..127) and 'sample' (a file). Answers the pad's state as track.drum_rack_get_state reads it. One undo step.

Flatten a track: render its output - its instrument or clips through its devices, fader, pan and sends, as bounce.land does (the whole track, or 'start'/'end' ticks; the file at 'out' or beside the project) - and REPLACE the track with an audio track of the same name at the same place playing the render, so the processing is committed and its CPU freed. Refused for a track whose document is too large to keep for an undo. One undo step puts the source track back with its clips, devices and settings. This command keeps its synchronous result contract for compatibility; use render.queue_bounce with operation flatten for a cancellable background job.

One folder addressed by its trk-<n> id: its mode (group or routing), the pinned and collapsed flags, the mixer channel it owns in routing mode, and every child with the channel that child is on. track.list, track.get_state and arrangement.get_state also carry each track's `folder`, so the relation is readable from the arrangement view of the song as well. Writes nothing.

Move every clip inside folder track 'folder' (its sub-folders too) by 'delta' ticks - the folder's part of the song as one block. With 'start' and 'end' only the clips starting in [start, end) move: one of the folder's summary clips, the spans its row draws. One undo step.

Collapse or expand a folder. This is the flag the track list's collapse would read; 0.3.0 persists it and drives it from here only (no chevron is drawn). Reversible through the ProjectJournal (the folder's own Track checkpoint).

One track addressed by its trk-<n> id: the number the track was given at creation, which it keeps until it is deleted. A malformed id is invalid_args; a well-formed id naming no live track is not_found. Addressing is scoped to the SONG container, so a track inside a nested container is not reachable by id.

An instrument track's MIDI input transform: channel (0 any), key_low / key_high, transpose, scale_mask (12 bits, C = bit 0; 0 no snapping), velocity_scale (%), velocity_offset, fixed_velocity (0 off), active.

Change what an instrument track does to LIVE MIDI input (not to clips): channel 0..16 (0 any), key_low / key_high (notes outside are dropped), transpose -48..48, scale_snap (true snaps to the scale context's notes, false stops), velocity_scale 1..400 %, velocity_offset -127..127, fixed_velocity 0..127 (0 off); a field left out keeps its value, 'reset' first restores the identity. A note-off follows its note-on, so a change while a key is held leaves no note hanging. One undo step.

Every track in the song container, with its stable trk-<n> id. The id is assigned at creation and persists in the project file. Addressing is scoped to the SONG container: a track inside a nested container (the <trackcontainer> a pattern track carries) is not reachable by id, exactly as it is not addressable by index.

Send an instrument track's notes out to the MIDI output 'port' (midi.device_list's writable ports) on 'channel' (1..16; 0 keeps each note's own) - an external synth, whose audio comes back on an audio track monitoring the input. 'enabled' false stops it and leaves every port. With only 'track' it reports the track's output. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).

Reorder a track: put it at `index` in the song's track list (0-based, the index track.list prints). Reversible through one recorded action step - control.undo puts the track back where it was, and the redo sends it forward again. Refuses an index outside the song rather than clamping it. A track that is not in the song container is refused too: the engine's own reorder erases-then-inserts, so a foreign pointer would be DUPLICATED into the song.

Every track in one list, for the track manager: id, index, name, type, colour, icon, muted, soloed, visible, folder, clip count, instrument, its mixer channel, that channel's device count and its processing load (cpu_percent, mixer.cpu_load's figure).
Put a track preset ('path') on a track of the same kind: its device, effects and settings; the track keeps its name. One undo step.
Save a track as a preset ('path', an absolute file - .xpf by custom): its device, effects and settings, without its mute and solo. Writes the file only.
Delete a track together with its clips. dry_run previews it.
Rename a track. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).

Arm or disarm a song track for recording. Arming starts a capture on the record route the track's position in the song maps to: the interleaved input channel named by 'input_channel' (default: the route's own index) is written to a 24-bit WAV and the take is journalled beside it, so a crash mid-take is recoverable (record.recovery_get_state). 'file' must be absolute and defaults to zene-take-trk<N>.wav beside this instance's recovery file. The frames a route records come from the engine's input path, so a route armed while nothing is staged records silence: record.input_get_state reports whether a capture device is open and how many frames are staged ('capture_capable', 'capture_open', 'capture_reason', 'input_frames_staged'). Arming writes a take file that stays on disk when the capture stops, so it has no complete inverse and control.undo refuses this command; stop the capture with this command again, armed: false, or with record.disarm_track. Disarming records no inverse either, because re-arming starts a NEW take.

Arm or disarm several song tracks for recording in one call - the mixer's Arm All. Each track in 'tracks' (trk-<n> ids) is armed or disarmed as track.set_arm does it, with its default take file and input channel; a track already armed is skipped, and a track that refuses (past the last record route, say) is listed in 'refused' with its reason while the others still go ahead. 'tracks' answers the ones changed, 'routes' each one's route reply. Arming writes take files that remain on disk when captures stop, so control.undo refuses this command; stop each route with record.disarm_track using its route id from 'routes'. Disarming records no inverse, as track.set_arm's does not.
Give a track the colour 'color' (#rrggbb), or none with 'color' empty - its header and clips take it. Saved with the project; one undo step.

Start every note of instrument track 'track' 'delay_ms' (0..500) milliseconds later - a slow instrument lined up, or a part sat behind the beat. Saved with the track. With only 'track' it reports it. One undo step.

Put a track into a folder, or take it out of one with an empty 'folder' (the container root). The folder relation is an attribute on the child's own <track> element and the child keeps its row in the flat track list, so this changes membership only. A folder is a track of type folder (track.add type=folder); a target that is not one is refused, typed, and a relation that would close a cycle is refused too.

Give a track an icon - one of the interface's icon names (drums, piano, automation, record, ...) - that its header shows instead of its type's; empty removes it. Saved with the project; one undo step.

Lock 'track' against editing ('locked' false unlocks it): its clips cannot be moved, resized, deleted or edited - by the mouse or by a command - until it is unlocked; mute, solo, arm, the mixer and automation stay open. Saved with the project; one undo step.

Route a track into a mixer channel: `channel` is a ch-<n> id (mixer.get_state lists them; the master is a channel too). What the track header's channel number and the Inspector's Mixer field set. Only instrument and sample tracks have a channel. Reversible: one control.undo puts the previous channel back. The reply names the previous channel.

Set how a track treats its live input: `off` never heard, `in` always heard, `auto` heard while the track is record-armed (track.set_arm) and not playing a clip. An audio track's input is its record route's input channel, played through the track's own devices, fader, pan and mixer channel; its default is off. An instrument track takes off or in (default in: every live note plays, as before); off keeps live notes out of the instrument. track.get_state reports `monitor`, and `monitor_frames` - the frames an audio track's gate has passed. Saved with the project only when not the default; reversible through the ProjectJournal (Track checkpoint).
Mute or unmute a track. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (the track's mute BoolModel checkpoint).

Pin or unpin a folder. This is the flag a non-scrolling pinned strip would read; 0.3.0 persists it and drives it from here only. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (the folder's own Track checkpoint).

Switch a folder between its two modes: false is GROUP - the organisational mode and the default - where each child keeps its own mixer channel, and true is ROUTING, where the folder takes a mixer channel of its own and every child's output is summed through it. Refused, typed, when the track is not a folder or when a routing folder has no children to sum.

Solo or unsolo a track. This is the product's whole solo action: the soloed track is unmuted and the others muted (TrackView drives that from the solo model), and the result carries the mute/solo state of every track.

A gap below 'track' in the track list, to divide the list into sections: 'height' in pixels (0 removes it, at most 200; 24 when a new spacer leaves it out) and an optional 'label' drawn in it. Not a track - it has no clips, device or channel - so it moves and goes with its track. Saved with the project; one undo step.
Show a track in the arranger or hide it ('visible'). Hiding mutes nothing: a hidden track still plays. Saved with the project; one undo step.
The tracks with a spacer below them, in track order: the track, its name, the spacer's height and label.
A track's versions: their names and the one playing ('active', empty before any is saved). Read only.
Forget the track's version 'name'. The track's clips stay as they are. One undo step.
Keep the track's clips as the version 'name' (replacing a version of that name) and make it the one playing. Saved with the project. One undo step.
Switch the track to its version 'name': the version playing is kept as it was left, and the track's clips become the named version's. One undo step puts both back.

Make exactly the members of a named visibility set visible and hide every other track of the song. A visibility flag is a VIEW flag: it mutes nothing and changes no render (the registered transcript proves that with a negative control). An unknown name is not_found, typed.

Every named visibility set this project holds, with its members and which one is active. Writes nothing. Each track's own `visible` flag is reported by track.list, track.get_state and arrangement.get_state.
Delete a named visibility set. The tracks' own visible flags are NOT changed: a set is a saved selection over them, and the flags are the project's own state. An unknown name is not_found, typed.

Create or replace a named visibility set: a named, id-based list of tracks that track.visibility_set_apply makes visible. Every named track must be live (a well-formed id naming none is not_found). Saved with the project, so a set survives project.save / project.open.

Make every track of the song visible again and leave no set active - the way back from track.visibility_set_apply. A view flag only: it mutes nothing and changes no render. One control.undo puts the previous flags and active set back.

Audition: play from 'position' (ticks), with every track but 'track' silenced when one is given - the arranger's audition tool while the button is held. transport.audition_stop puts the mutes, the transport and the play position back exactly. Not a project edit: nothing is recorded.
End an audition: the silenced tracks' own mutes, the transport and the play position come back as they were.
Playback position and transport flags.

The global swing: every note on an off-beat of 'grid' (16th or 8th) is played later by 'swing' (0..0.75) of a grid step - the notes themselves do not move. Saved with the project. With no arguments it reports the swing. One undo step.

Low-latency monitoring: with 'enabled', the devices whose latency is over 'max_ms' (0..100, 3 by default) stop processing on the chains of record-armed tracks, the channels they play into and the master ('scope' armed) - or on every chain ('scope' all) - so what you play is heard without their delay; off puts them back. Each call re-evaluates (arm a track, call again). Answers the devices it took out. Session state: nothing is saved or journalled.

How the metronome clicks: 'level' (0..2), 'accent' (the bar's first beat accented), 'sound' (classic, rim, clave or stick) and 'record_only' (click only while recording; a count-in clicks either way). transport.set_metronome switches it on. Preferences, kept in the config file. With no arguments it reports them. One undo step.

How notes are played back: 'chase' sounds a note playback starts, jumps or loops into the middle of - or that is already under the playhead when its track or clip is unmuted (off by default) - and 'offset_ms' (0..500) starts every note that much later, to line up a slow instrument. Preferences, kept in the config file. With no arguments it reports them. One undo step.
Stop every sounding note of every instrument now - the MIDI panic for a stuck note. Nothing in the project changes.
Start playback of the current song.

Disarm the punch region and forget it, leaving the timeline in the state a project that never punched has (which is also what gets written to the project file: the punch attributes are omitted). Refused, typed, when there is no region to clear. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Timeline checkpoint: the recorded inverse is transport.punch_set with the region that was cleared).

The transport's punch region: its range, whether it is armed, and `punch_active` - Timeline::punchCapturesAt() at the current play position, i.e. whether a capture starting here would be inside the region. Seek inside and outside the range to see the gate answer both ways. Writes nothing.
Punch at the play position, one action while a pass runs: 'edge' in starts the punch region here (to the song's end), out ends it here. Through transport.punch_set, so it is that command's undo step.

Set the transport's punch region - the tick range [start, end) that recording captures inside - and arm it (pass "enabled": false to set the range without arming it). An empty range is refused. The region is project state: it is written with the timeline (`punch0pos`/`punch1pos`/`punchstate` on the <timeline> element, and only when it is set, so a project that never punches saves the bytes it always has) and one control.undo takes it back off through the Timeline's own checkpoint. Both recording paths consult it frame-accurately: an armed region records only the frames inside [start, end), keeping the take aligned by writing silence outside. The Song Editor draws the region in its own ruler band with draggable handles and arms it with the Punch in/out button. Reversible through the ProjectJournal.

Start playback in record mode - the header's Record button dispatches this: sample tracks with recording enabled capture, and automation clips armed for recording write, while it plays (Song::playAndRecord). Starting from a stopped transport only: while the song is already playing the record mode cannot be switched on mid-run, so this is refused, typed - stop first. transport.stop ends it. Audio capture on a record route is armed per track (track.set_arm) and runs on its own.

How a recording pass starts and what it keeps: 'count_in_bars' (0..4 - the metronome clicks them before the play position, on or not), 'pre_roll_bars' (0..8 - played without the click), so the transport starts that many bars early and audio is captured only from the play position; 'mode' - the same choice for MIDI and audio - is overdub (a MIDI pass keeps the notes it plays over; an audio pass is mixed into the clip's audio, so the old audio stays audible), replace (a recorded note erases the notes already in the clip that it overlaps, at any pitch - notes only: the clip's controller lanes and all automation are kept; an audio pass replaces the clip's audio) or keep_history (an audio pass keeps the clip's earlier audio and the new pass as take lanes, the new pass active - comp.take_select chooses another; MIDI keeps notes as overdub does); the reply's 'mode_scope', 'midi_scope' and 'audio_scope' say so and 'modes' lists the choices. A field left out keeps its value; none reads them. A preference in the config file, not the project; a change is one undo step.
Move the play head to an absolute position in ticks.

Switch the metronome click on or off - the main toolbar's metronome toggle dispatches this. `previous` is the state before. Monitoring state, not project state: the project file does not carry it and nothing is journalled.
Set the song tempo in BPM.
Stop playback.

Add a tempo and/or time-signature event to the map, or replace the half it names at that tick (the other half is kept). Adding an event brings the map into force unless `active` is passed false: an event no timeline read would obey is a trap. Refused, typed, when the event fails the engine's own bounds or carries neither half, and a refusal writes nothing. With `ramp` (0.5.0) the tempo moves linearly from this event to the next tempo event instead of holding.

Remove every event AND switch the map off, in one step (one undo). Rejects an already empty, inactive map with invalid_args: an edit that changes nothing is not an edit. The inverse is the whole captured map, so this command names no single inverse command - the transaction records the map itself.

Beat mapping: make the tempo map follow a free performance. Each transient of the sample clip is taken as 'beats' (default 1) beats after the one before, and a tempo event is written at every one from the first hit on, so the grid's beats land on the playing (the audio itself is not changed). Events before the first hit stay; the map is switched on. One undo step.

The tempo map: every tempo and time-signature event, whether the map is in force, and what its queries answer AT THE PLAY HEAD - the tempo, the time signature and the elapsed seconds, read through the map's own ticks-to-time conversion. An empty or inactive map reports the global tempo at every position, and before the first event the global tempo is what is in force (docs/TEMPO-MAP.md).

Remove the tempo map event at an exact tick. A tick carrying no event is typed not_found. Removing the LAST event leaves an empty map, which is the pre-tempo-map engine: every tick answers the global tempo again.

Switch the tempo map's authority on or off WITHOUT editing its events: off, every tick answers the global tempo again and the stored events are still saved with the project; on, the timeline obeys them. A call that sets the state it already has is invalid_args.

How musician-facing positions and lengths read - the header's position, the Inspector's clip and note fields, the tempo map, the comp bounds: 'format' bars_beats (the default: "5.1.1" for a position, "1.0.0" for a one-bar length), ticks, or time (min:sec through the tempo map). Typed text is read in any of them. None given reads it. A preference in the config file, not the project; a change is one undo step.

The tuner's reading of the newest audio from its source: 'level' (RMS), and when a pitch is clear, 'hz', the nearest 'note' (A4, C#3...) with its MIDI 'key' and how many 'cents' off it is (-50..50) against reference_hz. 'clear' is false when the source is off, silent or has no single pitch.

What the tuner listens to - 'source': off (the default), input (the engine's input, what a recording takes) or master (the master output) - and its 'reference_hz' for A4 (400..480, 440 when never set). Session state: nothing is recorded or saved; while off the audio thread does one relaxed load.

Put a mixer channel into a group, so the group's fader scales it. Refused, typed, for ch-0 (master), for a channel already in this group, and for a channel that belongs to ANOTHER group - a channel is in at most one, which is what keeps 'soloing a member' single-valued; the refusal names the group holding it. With 'also' (0.5.0) the channel joins this group as well, and the groups' gains multiply. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (a recorded undo step).
Give every member channel of VCA group 'group' the colour 'color' (#rrggbb). One undo step.

Create a VCA / mix-and-edit group and return its vca-<n> id. A group owns one fader that scales every member mixer channel RELATIVE to the channel's own fader (moving it never writes a member's fader, which is what makes it exactly reversible), a mute, a solo, and - once vca.track_add has named them - a set of tracks whose media edits it locks together. A group holds no members at birth; add mixer channels with vca.assign and tracks with vca.track_add. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (the recorded inverse removes the group it created).

Set the same fade-in and/or fade-out length (ticks) on every locked AUDIO clip. A locked MIDI clip, or a fade longer than a locked clip, refuses the whole edit. The named clip is the anchor; a member track's clips that overlap the anchor's PRE-edit span are locked to it, a member with nothing there is reported in unlocked_tracks and a gone track in skipped_tracks. Refused, typed, when the group's phase lock is off, when the anchor's track is not in the edit set, or when the set has fewer than two live tracks - and every edit refusal is checked for every locked clip first, so a refusal writes nothing. One control.undo reverses every member.

Move a clip to an absolute tick position AND move every other member of the group's edit set by the SAME delta, so the members stay locked to one timeline (this is the phase-locked multitrack edit). The named clip is the anchor; a member track whose clips overlap the anchor's pre-command span is moved by the delta, a member with nothing there is reported in unlocked_tracks, and a member whose track is gone in skipped_tracks. Refused, typed, when the group's phase lock is off, when the anchor's track is not in the edit set, or when the set has fewer than two live tracks. One control.undo returns every moved clip. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (a composite Clip checkpoint covering every clip the lock moved).

Slip the anchor's content to `offset` and every locked clip's content by the SAME delta; no clip's position or length moves. The named clip is the anchor; a member track's clips that overlap the anchor's PRE-edit span are locked to it, a member with nothing there is reported in unlocked_tracks and a gone track in skipped_tracks. Refused, typed, when the group's phase lock is off, when the anchor's track is not in the edit set, or when the set has fewer than two live tracks - and every edit refusal is checked for every locked clip first, so a refusal writes nothing. One control.undo reverses every member.

Split every locked clip at one song tick (`position`), so the members are cut at exactly the same place - the phase-locked multitrack split. A locked clip the cut does not fall inside is left whole; the anchor must contain it. The named clip is the anchor; a member track's clips that overlap the anchor's PRE-edit span are locked to it, a member with nothing there is reported in unlocked_tracks and a gone track in skipped_tracks. Refused, typed, when the group's phase lock is off, when the anchor's track is not in the edit set, or when the set has fewer than two live tracks - and every edit refusal is checked for every locked clip first, so a refusal writes nothing. One control.undo reverses every member.

Trim the anchor's start edge to `start` (and its end to `end`) and move every locked clip's edges by the SAME deltas, holding each clip's audio at its song position (clip.trim's head-trim rule). `delta_start`/`delta_end` report the deltas. The named clip is the anchor; a member track's clips that overlap the anchor's PRE-edit span are locked to it, a member with nothing there is reported in unlocked_tracks and a gone track in skipped_tracks. Refused, typed, when the group's phase lock is off, when the anchor's track is not in the edit set, or when the set has fewer than two live tracks - and every edit refusal is checked for every locked clip first, so a refusal writes nothing. One control.undo reverses every member.

One group addressed by its vca-<n> id: the name, the fader value, the gain actually published to the members (0 when the group is muted), the mute and solo flags, the phase lock, every member channel with the gain it is scaled by, and the edit set with the ids whose track no longer exists reported separately as missing_tracks. Writes nothing.

Every group of the mix with its whole state: the fader and the gain published from it, the mute and solo flags, the phase lock, the member mixer channels with the gain each one is being scaled by right now, and the edit set as trk-<n> ids (with the ids that no longer name a live track separated out). Writes nothing.

Delete a group. Its member channels play at their own faders again (the published gain is reset), and the edit set goes with the group. The delete is EXACTLY reversible: one control.undo re-creates the group with its id, name, fader, mute, solo, phase-lock flag, member channels and edit tracks.

Rename a group. The name is what a group is called in the project file's <vcagroup> element and what its fader, mute and solo display names are built from; it is not an address, so vca-<n> ids are unaffected. An empty name is refused, typed. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (a recorded undo step).

Set a group's fader (0..2, 1.0 is unity and 2.0 is +6 dB). The fader SCALES every member channel relative to the channel's own fader - no member model is written - so moving it and moving it back leaves every member bit-identical, and a member keeps the value the user set for it. The result reports the gain actually published to the members, which is 0 while the group is muted. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (the group's fader model checkpoint).

Choose what a group links on its members: 'gain' (its fader), 'mute' and 'solo', each on by default; 'suspended' turns every link off while keeping the choice. A field left out keeps its value. One undo step.

Mute or unmute a group. Mute is a gain of zero published from the group, NOT the members' own mute models - so muting a group silences every member, a soloed member of a muted group stays silent, and each member's own mute state survives the pair untouched. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (the group's mute model checkpoint).

Put a group inside another ('parent', a vca-<n>; empty or left out takes it out): the parent's gain - and every group's above it - scales this group's members too. A loop, or nesting deeper than 8, is refused. One undo step.

Switch a group's phase lock on or off. With the lock ON, a media edit made on one of the group's tracks is applied to every other member at the same source position (see vca.edit_move); with it OFF the membership is kept but the takes can be edited independently again. The default for a new group is ON. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (a recorded undo step).

Solo or unsolo a group. Soloing a group makes exactly its members audible (the same exclusive solo a channel has, so soloing a group clears any other group's), and clearing the flag restores the pre-solo mute state of every channel. Reversible: one undo step restores every group's solo flag, channel mute and transient pre-solo cache. The transaction inverse carries that full state for replay even after its journal step is evicted.

Add a track to a group's edit set, so media edits on it are locked to every other member's. Membership is by the track's STABLE trk-<n> id and is recorded on the GROUP, not on the track; the group does not have to be a mixer group of anything (a group can be an edit group alone). Survives save/reload (the group's <vcagroup> element carries an <edittrack track="n"/> child per member). Reversible through the ProjectJournal (a recorded undo step).

Take a track out of a group's edit set. No clip moves: the track simply stops being locked to the others. A track that is not in the set is REFUSED rather than silently accepted. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (a recorded undo step).

Take a mixer channel out of a group. The channel plays at its own fader again (its published gain returns to unity) and keeps that fader's value throughout. A channel that is not a member of this group is REFUSED rather than silently accepted, so a wrong id cannot look like a success. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (a recorded undo step).

Attach the video file 'path' to the project (one video per project: an attached one is replaced), its first frame shown at song tick 'offset' (0 when left out). FFmpeg reads its frame rate, length, size and whether it has sound. The video window and the arranger's video lane follow it. Saved with the project (the path absolute); one undo step.
Take the video off the project (the file is left alone). One undo step.

Decode the video's sound to a 32-bit float stereo WAV - 'out', or '<video>-audio.wav' next to the project (next to the video while the project is unsaved), numbered when taken - and put it on a new audio track at the video's offset. Runs to the end before it answers - or, with 'background' true, decodes on a worker listed in the task area (task.list: its progress, and task.cancel stops it) and answers at once with the 'task' id; the track then lands when the decode completes. One undo step removes the track; the WAV stays on disk.

The project's video: whether one is attached, its 'path' (and whether the file still 'exists'), the song tick it starts at ('offset', also in seconds) and ends at ('end'), its 'fps', 'duration' (seconds), 'width', 'height' and 'has_audio'.
Move the video to start at song tick 'offset'. Saved with the project; one undo step.

Show the video window ('shown' false hides it; it toggles when left out): the project's video, following play, seeks and loops - frames are dropped rather than late when decoding falls behind - with its timecode (HH:MM:SS:FF). Decoding runs on its own thread. Interface state.

What a screen reader is told without asking: 'level' all (errors, refused edits, recording starting and stopping, a project saved or opened, a finished job - the default), errors (errors and refusals only) or off. The same message is never spoken twice within a second, and values are spoken only for the focused control, never for meters or automation. A preference in the config file (ui/announcements); one undo step.
Show a cross-hair cursor across the arranger - a vertical and a horizontal guide through the pointer - or hide it ('enabled'; toggles when left out). A preference in the config file; one undo step.

Pin one frame of a sample clip's audio to a timeline position (a warp marker). The clip keeps its markers in source-frame order and the engine refuses a marker that would reuse a source frame or put the set out of order - nothing is written in that case. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

The warp map of a sample clip: its markers (the source frame each one pins and the clip-relative timeline offset it lands on, in the order the engine holds them), its tempo mode, its declared source tempo and the engine's marker cap. Read-only.

Move the warp marker that pins a given source frame to a new timeline offset, keeping it pinned to that same frame of the audio. The new offset must stay strictly between the marker's neighbours. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

Quantise a sample clip's audio: its transients (the onset rule detect.* uses) become warp markers, each moved 'strength' (0..1, default 1) of the way to the nearest 'grid' step (ticks, default 48 = 1/4) from where the clip plays it now; the new markers replace the old ones (at most 128, in order). The audio is not changed - the warp is, so warp.stretch picks how it sounds. Refused not_found when the audio has no transient. One undo step (Clip checkpoint).

Delete the warp marker that pins a given source frame, leaving the rest of the map in place. Removing the last marker leaves the clip unwarped, so its mapping is the linear one again. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

Set a sample clip's warp map: replace the whole marker list ('markers'; an empty array clears it), choose the tempo mode ('follow' the project tempo, or 'source' - the clip leads with the tempo it was recorded at) and/or declare that source tempo in BPM. One call is one undoable step. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

Choose how a warped sample clip renders its rate change: 're_pitch' (the default, and what the engine has always done - the rate goes to the resampler and the pitch moves with it, so a 2x warp is an octave up; the old name 'resample' is accepted), 'preserve_pitch' (the same rate is rendered by the WSOLA stretcher, AudioStretcher, at its default parameters: the clip lasts as long as the mapping says and keeps its own pitch), 'tones' (the same WSOLA stretch with its alignment reach doubled to ±256 frames, for monophonic and tonal material), 'texture' (the same stretch with half the grain, for polyphonic and ambient material), or one of the two Rubber Band-backed modes (Q050-036): 'beats' (R3 restricted to its single short window - the crispest timing at some spectral cost) and 'complex' (R3's full multi-resolution settings, the quality the old name 'rubberband' - also accepted - has always rendered). A build without librubberband refuses those two, and a file that asks for one still loads and renders through WSOLA for the pass in which both of the clip's voices are busy. Refused for a clip that renders linearly - with no marker and no source tempo there is no rate change to render. Reversible through the ProjectJournal (Clip checkpoint).

Walk the main window's controls and count those a screen reader would announce with no name, no role (a bare client or pane) or, for a control that shows a value, no value, and those Tab cannot reach; with 'fill', give each nameless one the name it already carries (its constructed name, its parameter's, its tooltip, its text). Lists, at most 50 of each, the controls with nothing to name them by and those with no role or value. The interface fills names this way once at start. Theme 17's staged audit: 'checks' picks the checks to run - name, role, value, focus (the controls Tab cannot reach, listed) and duplicates (controls announced alike with no named group, description or role to tell them apart) - all when left out; the reply's 'summary' counts each check's findings. Interface state.

How the interface looks, from the next start: 'scale' (0.5..3), the one interface zoom - text, icons and controls scale together; an explicit QT_SCALE_FACTOR still wins - 'palette' (dark, high_contrast - text at 7:1 on every surface - or light), 'accessible', accessible mode: larger click targets, strong focus rings, the high-contrast palette and reduced motion, and 'workspace' (standard or touch): the touch workspace holds the launcher's cells, scene and stop buttons to at least 44 x 44 Qt logical pixels at 100% zoom. Kept for older callers: 'font_scale' sets the zoom when 'scale' is not given, and 'density' sets accessible mode (standard off; comfortable or touch on) when 'accessible' is not given - it does not choose the workspace. A field left out keeps its value; none reads them. A preference in the config file; a change is one undo step.
Open Help > Ask (app.ask in a window), asking 'question' at once when given; 'answers' is how many it found (an open one is raised and asked). Offline.
Put a panel shown in its own window (window.detach) back in the shell.

Since 0.5.0 a no-op kept for compatibility: there is no workspace to attach a window to (secondary windows float; the editors are shell panels). `detached` answers true - the state that holds. Interface state only.

Open the command palette (non-modally) - View > Command Palette and Ctrl+Shift+P dispatch this. It lists every enabled menu action with its menu path and shortcut, plus every command that needs no argument, filters them as you type and runs the highlighted one: a menu entry triggers the real action (its dialog included), a command entry is dispatched through the registry. `entries` is how many it offers.

Show shell panel 'panel' (window.get_state's panel ids) in a window of its own - one that can sit on a second monitor; it stays there whatever view is chosen until window.attach or its window is closed. With 'screen' (an index into the connected screens, 0 = the first) its window moves onto that screen, also when it already floats. Interface state: not recorded.

Since 0.5.0 a no-op kept for compatibility: every secondary window already floats as its own top-level window, and the editors are shell panels, not windows. `detached` is always true. Interface state only.

Move the keyboard focus into shell panel 'panel' (window.get_state's panel ids; a hidden one is shown first), or to the 'next' / 'previous' open panel from the focused one (the default is next) - F6 and Shift+F6. Interface state.

Put the main window into fullscreen or take it out - View > Fullscreen dispatches this. With no `enabled` it toggles. Leaving fullscreen restores the maximised or normal state the window had. Interface state only.

The shell's layout: `view` (arrange, mix or edit); `panels`, one {id, title, region, visible, available, shortcut, mounted} per panel, where region is left, center, bottom or right and available says whether the current view offers it; `focused`, the panel that last took keyboard focus; `launcher`, whether the clip launcher sits beside the view's main panel; `editors`, one {editor, visible, panel} entry per window.toggle name; `tools`, one {name, command, editor, home} per tool that opens in a window of its own (the footer's Tools menu: the command that opens it, and its window.toggle editor when it has one); `regions`, per side region (left, bottom, right) the panel `open` there and the `tabs` its tab strip offers in this view; `footer`, how the footer's switches fit its width (labelled, compact, or overflowing into its More button); `note_editor`, the note editor's view (window.note_editor_set's reply); and `selection`, what the Inspector and the Device panel show (window.select's reply). Read-only. Refused `requires` in a process with no interface.
The header's buttons - name, text, command, shown or not - and the user's choices (hidden names, extra command buttons).

Customise the header: 'hidden' lists button names to hide (the rest show), 'extra' adds buttons that run registry commands ([{command, label}], commands that need no arguments). A field not given is kept. Kept in the config file; one undo step.

Q050-340: open the Input Meters window (an open one is raised): a labelled bar for every capture channel the input carries ('In 1', 'In 2', ...) and one for every record-armed track's selected input ('<track> - In <n>'), -60..0 dB with the mixer's fall-off. The answer is what the window shows now: 'channels' and 'armed', each meter's 'label', 'input_channel' (0-based), 'level_db' (-120 for silence) and, for an armed track, its record 'route'. meter.inputs reads the same levels for an agent without taking the window's. A display.

Open the editable item list of a canvas beside it, or close it ('visible'; toggles when left out) - 'surface': notes (the open note editor's notes, with the expression lane's value), controller (the controller lane's points), xy (the open XY pad's two axes), comp (the take lanes' comp segments), clips (the arrangement's clips) or automation (the automation editor's points: position and value as a share of the control's range). Every cell edit, Insert and Delete in the list runs the canvas's own command (note.edit, note.add, note.remove_many, clip.controllers_set, rack.macro_set, comp.select, clip.move, clip.resize, clip.add, clip.delete, automation.move_point), one undo step each; selection follows the canvas both ways. Answers the list: {surface, visible, title, columns: [{id, title, editable}], rows: [{id, <column>: text}] (at most 200), count}. Ctrl+Shift+L on a canvas. Interface state.
Open a large clock: the play position in bars, beats and ticks and in minutes and seconds, big enough to read across the room (an open one is raised instead). A display.

Switch to the saved layout 'name'; answers window.get_state's view of the result and the parts it put back ('captures'). It becomes the personal layout: one a project's layout had put aside is dropped. Interface state, as window.set_view is: not recorded.

The personal library's layout names, its limit, whether the project remembers a layout of its own ('project_layout', window.layout_project_*), and whether a project's layout is on screen with the personal one put aside ('project_layout_shown').

Put back the layout the project remembers; answers window.get_state's view of the result and the parts it put back ('captures'). The personal layout on screen before is put aside and comes back when a project without a layout of its own opens, a new project starts, or at the next start (window.layout_list's 'project_layout_shown'). Interface state: not recorded. Refused NotFound when it remembers none.
Forget the layout the project remembers (the personal layouts are kept). One undo step; refused NotFound when it remembers none.

Remember the window layout on screen with the project (the same parts window.layout_save keeps: 'captures' lists them), replacing the one it remembered ('replaced'). Saved with the project and put back when it opens; one undo step ('changed' false, and no step, when it remembered just this one).
Forget the saved layout 'name'. One undo step.

Save the window layout - the view, the open, pinned and floating panels and the splitter sizes ('captures' lists the parts kept) - under 'name' in the personal library, replacing one of that name ('replaced') unless 'replace' is false, when a name in use is refused. At most 32 are kept ('max_layouts'), in the config file; one undo step.

Open Edit > Live Code (non-modally): the source editor and the id/hook/budget a scheduled Lua script is made with, Schedule and Cancel Schedule running livecode.schedule / livecode.unschedule, Load Source reading livecode.get_source, and the schedule table from livecode.get_state (id, hook, budget, bytes, fire and error counts, last failure). A compile refusal is shown in the panel and leaves the schedule that was active in place; Undo runs control.undo, which restores a replaced script or rearms a cancelled one. The panel's help text states the Lua-state, source, count, poll and memory bounds. `schedules` is how many schedules it lists.

The mixer view's modes, set and answered: 'sends_on_faders' (a ch-<n> return, or empty for the channel faders) makes every channel's fader drive its send to that return - a banner across the mixer names it, every fader is labelled with what it drives, and a channel with no send there keeps a dimmed, still 'No send' fader in place; the answer adds 'sends_on_faders_name' (the return's name) and 'faders' (per channel, what its fader drives: volume, send or no_send - the return's own fader and the master's stay volume); 'folded' answers the channel strips a collapsed folder hides (track.folder_set_collapsed folds). MX-005: 'selected_channels' (ch-<n> ids, never the master) are the channels the 'selected' filter shows - interface state, never saved, forgotten when the mixer is cleared for another project; a Ctrl+click on a strip adds or removes its channel, and the mode bar's 'Pick...' chooses them; the answer lists them in mixer order. The view options, kept in the config file (ui/mixerview): 'show_sends', 'show_pan', 'show_number', 'show_meter_info', 'show_inserts', 'show_macros' (a strip's sections - the meter line is the gain reduction and the clip light, the inserts are listed by name, the macros are the rack's first four as knobs), 'show_console' (Q050-088: the Console section - knobs and switches for the channel's trim, polarity, EQ and its Console's drive and glue compressor, each running mixer.console_strip; off by default, hidden in the routing view and the compact density), 'strip_width' (narrow / normal / wide), 'filter' (all / instruments / audio / returns / used - the channels a track plays into or a send reaches -, selected), 'meter_mode' (peak - after the fader -, rms, pre_fader) and 'meter_scale' (db42 - the default range -, db60, db24, linear); MX-128, the meters' ballistics: 'meter_falloff' (fast - the default, about 116 dB/s -, medium - about 26 dB/s -, slow - about 12 dB/s, a peak programme meter's fall) and 'peak_hold' (how long the peak line holds: off, 1.5s - the default -, 3s, 6s). Theme 16: 'view' (mix - levels, pan and processing, the default -, routing - each strip lists where its signal comes from and goes by name, the sends row always shown, inserts and macros left to the mix view) and 'density' (expanded - the default, every section the options show -, compact - no inserts, no macros, in the mix view no sends row, routing on one line); a mode bar across the mixer shows and sets both, the filter and the modes. The answer adds 'strips': per channel its 'type' (master, return, group, track, channel), 'format' (stereo, LCR, Quad, 5.1, 7.1), 'inputs' and 'outputs' (by name; each output with amount, pre_fader, enabled), 'hardware' (its hardware output's label, empty for none) and 'states' (afl, pfl, solo_safe, surround_pan, cue, hardware_insert). Interface state: nothing is journalled.

Open Edit > Modulators (non-modally): the modulation layer's modulators as modulator.get_state reports them, Add LFO / Remove, the selected one's shape and rate, the parameters it drives and a Bind row over a mixer channel's effects, each running the modulator.* command it names. `rows` is how many modulators it lists.

Drive the note editor's VIEW - what the editor's header and keys set - and answer its state (the same object window.get_state reports as `note_editor`). Every field is optional: `clip` opens that MIDI clip in the editor (what double-clicking it does); `tool` is one of FL Studio's piano-roll tools - draw (P), select (E), slice (C), erase (the Delete tool, D), audition (the Play tool, Y), paint (B: drag to lay a note on every grid cell) or mute (T); `grid` the snap in ticks (1 = off); `fold` none, scale, used or drums (the keys the track names - key_names.* - and the used ones); `lane` the expression lane (velocity, pan, chance, timbre, pressure, pitch, release, spread, repeats); `ghosts` shows the track's other clips; `color_mode` colours notes by velocity, pitch or track; `keep_in_scale` moves drawn and dragged notes to the nearest key of the scale; `controller_lane` (cc:<n>, pitchbend, aftertouch, program; empty for the note lane) shows that controller curve of the clip under the notes (clip.controllers_set edits it); `new_length` (ticks; 0 the last drawn) and `new_velocity` are what a clicked note gets; `audio_behind` draws an audio clip's waveform behind the notes (a clip id, auto - the first one sounding with the clip - or empty); `zoom` is pixels per tick; `fit` zooms to the clip and centres its notes (after the panel is shown); `zoom_to_selection` fits the selected notes, or the clip when none is (the Z key); `reveal` (default true) brings the note editor panel into view. Interface state, not project state: nothing is journalled - the notes themselves are edited through note.*. Refused `requires` in a process with no interface.

MX-137: open the Phase Scope (an open one is raised and moved) on mixer channel 'channel' (a ch-<n> id; left out, the open one's channel, else the master): a goniometer of the channel's newest frames - mono stands up the middle, out of phase lies flat, the left channel alone leans left - beside its phase correlation (+1 mono, 0 wide, -1 out of phase). The answer names the channel ('channel', 'channel_name'), its 'correlation' now and 'frames_seen', the frames the view's tap has been fed since it was pointed at the channel (it grows while the engine runs and the channel is not muted). Closing the window stops the tap. A display.

Pin a side panel ('panel': browser, inspector, devices, mixer, detail...) open in every view that offers it, or unpin it ('pinned' false) - the pin button in the panel's header. Kept with the layout (a preference, not project state). Refused for the arranger (always a main panel) and the launcher; a pinned mixer or note editor is still the main panel of its own view.

Open Edit > Progression (non-modally): the named progressions the catalogue holds, each SPELLED OUT in the selected scale (chord.progression_list with `scale`/`root`/`octave`), what the selected one writes, and a Write button that runs chord.progression_generate on the clip the shell's selection names. The scale, key and octave are the panel's own choice; they are not written back to the scale context. `rows` is how many progressions it lists.
