Open the Sample Editor on an audio clip (what the clip menu's Sample Editor... does), or bring its open one forward, and set its VIEW: `from` and `to` select the source frames [from, to) - End exclusive, as sample.edit_range takes them, clamped to the source and swapped if reversed; `unit` is what its Start, End and Length fields read in (time, bars_beats - at the song's tempo from the clip's start - or samples); `zoom` zooms the waveform in or out, to the selection, or to all of it. The reply is the editor's state, the range also as the fields show it. Interface state, not project state: nothing is journalled - sample.edit_range edits the audio. Refused `requires` in a process with no interface.

Write a PNG of the main window - or, with `window: "active"`, of the top-level window that has focus (a dialog, the palette) - to the absolute `path`. For an agent that has to SEE the interface it drives: layout, labels and state as rendered, which no read command reports. Works under the offscreen platform. `width`/`height` are the image's.

Select what the Inspector and the Device panel show - what clicking a track header, a clip or a mixer strip does. `clip` (clip-<n>) selects that clip and its track; otherwise `channel` (ch-<n>) selects a mixer channel on its own; otherwise `track` (trk-<n>) selects a track, and an empty `track` clears the selection; no argument just answers. The reply is {track, clip, channel, inspector, devices}: the Inspector's {track, clip, channel, name, muted, soloed} and the Device panel's {track, channel, cards: [{target, plugin, name, enabled, parameters, shown}], modulators} - a track's own mixer channel (not the master) is drawn after its devices, with the modulators beside the inserts they drive. Interface state, not project state: nothing is journalled. Refused `requires` in a process with no interface.

Switch the shell's view - the footer's view words, View > Arrange/Mix/Edit and Alt+1/2/3 dispatch exactly this. `view` is arrange (the arranger timeline in the centre), mix (the mixer) or edit (the note editor); each view keeps its own side panels. `changed` is false when the view was already showing. Interface state, not project state: nothing is journalled. Refused `requires` in a process with no interface.
Open the Settings dialog (non-modally) - Edit > Settings dispatches this. What the dialog changes on OK is what settings.set writes; this only shows it.

Open Help > Keyboard Shortcuts (non-modally): every menu action that carries a shortcut, with its menu path and the registry command it declares, read from the live menus and filterable. Read-only: it lists shortcuts, it does not remap them. `entries` is how many shortcuts it lists.

Open File > Start Hub (non-modally): start a new project, empty or from a template, reopen a recent one, and the Learn section (the command palette, the keyboard shortcuts page, the online manual). Its buttons run project.new, project.open and those window verbs through the registry. It never opens by itself at startup. `recent` and `templates` are how many it offers.
Keep the main window above other programs' windows, or not ('enabled'; toggles when left out). Its maximised or fullscreen state is kept. Interface state.

Open Edit > Tempo Map (non-modally): the tempo map's events as transport.tempo_map_get reports them, its Active switch, and Add at playhead / Remove / Clear, each running the transport.tempo_map_* command it names. `rows` is how many events it lists.

Tidy the floating windows - detached panels, dialogs (not a modal prompt), plug-in windows - over the main window's screen: 'cascade' (the default: stepped from its top left corner, starting again before the middle) or 'tile' (a grid). Interface state.

Show or hide one shell panel or floating window - the View menu, the footer's panel buttons and Tools menu, a region's tabs, Alt+I/B/D/E/M/A/P/L, the MDI-era Ctrl+1..7 and Edit > Scales and keymaps dispatch exactly this. `editor` is a panel id (arranger, launcher, detail, devices, inspector, browser, mixer, automation, pattern), a 0.4.0 editor name (song = arranger, piano_roll = detail, clip_launcher = launcher), or a floating window (controller_rack, project_notes, microtuner, classic_piano_roll, perform - perform mode, the launcher's live show window). A panel shares its region with others, so showing it hides the region's previous panel; a view's main panel cannot be hidden (it stays visible); a panel the current view does not offer is revealed by switching to the Arrange view. `visible` is the state afterwards, `panel` the panel id (empty for a window), `view` the view afterwards. Interface state, not project state: nothing is journalled. Refused `requires` in a process with no interface.
Open the tool menu at the pointer: the arranger's tools and the note editor's, each running arrangement.set_tool or window.note_editor_set. Headless, nothing is shown and the entries are answered.

Open the tuner: the note nearest the pitch of its source (the input, unless tuner.set chose another), the cents off it and a needle (an open one is raised instead); closing it switches the tuner off. A display.

Open Edit > Undo History (non-modally): the undo stack as control.undo_depth reports it, Undo and Redo buttons that run control.undo / control.redo, and the command record control.transactions keeps, newest first. An edit made directly in an editor is undone by Undo but is not in that record, and the panel says so. `rows` is how many recorded commands it lists.
Show this version's release notes (app.whats_new) and remember they were shown, so the start does not show them again until the next version.
The workflows in the library in use, with their steps, and which library that is ('scope': shared or project).

Start recording workflow 'name': every command that changes something from now on (not undo, redo or the workflow commands) becomes one of its steps, with its arguments, until workflow.record_stop. Refused while another is being recorded. The recording shows in the header and the Workflows menu, and in workflow.status's 'recording'; 'replaces' says a saved workflow of that name will be replaced when it stops.

Stop recording and save the workflow as workflow.save would (refused when nothing was done; a refused save keeps recording, nothing lost). Commands past the 64th step are not kept: 'dropped' counts them. One undo step.
Forget workflow 'name' from the library in use. One undo step.

Resume the last workflow run, which stopped at a failing step: run that step again and the rest, or with 'skip' leave it out and run the rest - the steps as the workflow is saved now. Acknowledged at once ('queued', 'from' 0-based, 'retried' or 'skipped' the step's number) and run as workflow.run runs; workflow.status adds up what applied and what was skipped over the resumes. Refused when the last run did not stop at a failure. Each step records and undoes as itself; this command records nothing of its own.

Run workflow 'name': acknowledged at once ('queued' steps), then each step runs through the registry on the next turn of the event loop, in order, stopping at the first that fails - workflow.status reports the outcome ('stopped_at', -1 when every step ran; which step failed and why, which applied and stay applied, which did not run) and the interface shows it in a report with Retry and Skip (workflow.resume). Each step records and undoes as itself; this command records nothing of its own. One workflow runs at a time.

Save a workflow: 'steps' is a list of {command, args} run in order by workflow.run (1..64 steps, every command registered, none a workflow.* one). Replaces a workflow of that name ('replaced' says so); at most 64 are kept. The Workflows menu gains an action for it. Kept in the library in use ('scope': shared, in the config file, or project, saved with the project - workflow.set_scope); one undo step.

Choose where workflows are kept: 'shared' (the default - one library in the config file, for every project) or 'project' (each project's own, saved with it). The other library is kept as it is, and comes back when it is chosen again. The ui/workflows.scope setting; one undo step ('changed' false, and no step, when it was already so).

The last workflow run: 'state' (idle, running, done), and once done how many steps ran, where it stopped ('stopped_at'), each step's outcome, the failed step with its reason and arguments ('failed'), which steps applied, were skipped or did not run, whether it can be resumed and the outcome as a sentence ('message'); 'recording' says whether a workflow is being recorded (its name and steps so far).
